library.hook: Pasting someone else's material into a tool is a licensing decision.
library.message: A licensed report, a client's document, a paywalled article — feeding it to a third-party service may exceed what your licence permits, regardless of how the output is used.
library.action: Do this: check whether you have the right to share the input, not just use it.

library.title: Client Contract Clauses
library.hook: Some of your existing client contracts already restrict AI. You've signed them.
library.message: Clauses on subcontracting, data processing, confidentiality and approved locations often catch AI tools without naming them. The restriction predates the technology and still binds you.
library.action: Do this: check the contract before using AI on client work. Ask legal if the wording is ambiguous.

library.title: Regulated Decisions
library.hook: Some decisions are constrained by law regardless of how good the model is.
library.message: Hiring, credit, insurance, healthcare, education access and safety-critical judgements carry legal requirements for human involvement, explanation and appeal in many markets.
library.action: Do this: if a decision affects someone's rights or livelihood, check the rules before automating any part of it.

library.title: Disclosure Obligations
library.hook: Sometimes you have to tell the client. Know when.
library.message: Disclosure is required when a contract says so, when a regulator requires it, when the client asked, or when a reasonable person would want to know. Increasingly, silence is the thing that damages trust.
library.action: Do this: raise it early and matter-of-factly. Late disclosure always looks worse.

library.title: Audit Trail Requirements
library.hook: If a decision matters, someone will ask how it was made. Log accordingly.
library.message: You need the input, the tool and version, the output, who reviewed it, what they changed, and who approved it. Reconstructing this a year later from memory is not possible.
library.action: Do this: save the prompt and output alongside the deliverable, not in your chat history.

library.title: Records and Discovery
library.hook: Your prompt history is discoverable. Write as if it will be read aloud.
library.message: In litigation, regulatory inquiry or internal investigation, AI conversations are evidence like any other record. Speculation, frustration and shortcuts typed into a chat window can all surface later.
library.action: Do this: don't type anything into a prompt you wouldn't put in an email.

library.title: Agent Permissions Review
library.hook: Every credential you give an agent is one it can use badly at speed.
library.message: Agents don't misuse access maliciously; they misuse it by misunderstanding. Broad permissions turn a small misinterpretation into a large, fast, well-logged mistake.
library.action: Do this: review what each agent can actually reach. Remove anything it hasn't needed this month.

library.title: Unlogged Agents
library.hook: An automation nobody can see is treated as an incident, not an initiative.
library.message: If it runs without logging, we can't tell what it did, prove it didn't do something, or stop it cleanly. Undocumented automation is the single hardest thing to investigate.
library.action: Do this: register any automation you've built. Retrospective registration is fine; hiding it isn't.

library.title: Approval Gates in Workflows
library.hook: Put the human checkpoint where the human can still change the outcome.
library.message: A review step after the email has sent or the record has updated isn't oversight, it's notification. The gate belongs before the irreversible action, not after it.
library.action: Do this: map your automation and mark the last point where a person can still say no.

library.title: Kill Switch Drill
library.hook: If you can't stop it in sixty seconds, you don't control it.
library.message: Every running automation needs a documented way to halt it, known to more than one person, tested at least once. The middle of an incident is not when to discover the switch doesn't work.
library.action: Do this: find the kill switch for one automation you rely on. Test it.

library.title: Scope Creep in Automation
library.hook: It started as a script to tidy a spreadsheet. Now it emails clients.
library.message: Automation grows by small reasonable extensions, each too minor to warrant review, until something material is running with no owner, no logging and no approval behind it.
library.action: Do this: if your automation now does something you didn't originally approve, re-register it.

library.title: Connected Accounts Inventory
library.hook: You'd be surprised what still has live access to your systems.
library.message: Trial integrations, an agent from a finished project, a tool a former colleague connected. Each holds credentials, and each is a path in that nobody is watching.
library.action: Do this: review the connected accounts list for your team and revoke what isn't in use.

library.title: Testing Before Production
library.hook: Before an automation touches real data, it has to survive a test.
library.message: Run it on a copy. Feed it malformed input, empty fields, and the weird edge case someone will eventually produce. Confirm the failure behaviour is safe, not just that success works.
library.action: Do this: never let production be the first realistic test.

library.title: Reporting an AI Mistake
library.hook: When something goes wrong, the first hour matters more than the blame.
library.message: Tell us what you asked, what came back, what you did with it, and who might be affected. We're looking for the pattern, not the culprit. Fast reporting has never cost anyone here.
library.action: Do this: use the report template. Send it before you've worked out the whole story.

library.title: Prompt Injection in the Wild
library.hook: Instructions can hide inside the documents your AI reads.
library.message: Text in a PDF, an email footer or a web page can tell the model to ignore its rules, reveal earlier content, or take an action. The user never sees it; the model does.
library.action: Do this: treat any AI summary of untrusted content as suspect. Never let it trigger an action automatically.

library.title: Deepfake and Voice Verification
library.hook: A familiar voice on the phone is no longer proof of anything.
library.message: Voice and video cloning now works from seconds of public audio. The request will sound urgent, plausible, and exactly like someone you know, because in every observable way it is.
library.action: Do this: verify unusual requests through a second channel you initiate. Always, no exceptions for seniority.

library.title: AI in Meetings
library.hook: Notetakers are useful, and they're also recording devices in the room.
library.message: Default settings often join meetings, transcribe everything, and store it somewhere searchable. Participants frequently don't know, and external attendees almost never consented.
library.action: Do this: announce the bot before recording starts, and turn it off for sensitive conversations.

library.title: Skills Self-Assessment
library.hook: Ten minutes of honesty about what you can actually do with these tools.
library.message: The assessment isn't a test you pass or fail. It tells you which capabilities you have, which you think you have, and what the next level of use requires from you.
library.action: Do this: complete it honestly. Inflated answers only cost you the training you'd benefit from.

library.title: Team AI Maturity Review
library.hook: Once a quarter, look at what your team is actually doing with AI.
library.message: Not adoption numbers — practice. What's genuinely working, what's quietly been abandoned, where people are working around a rule, and what's drifted since the last conversation.
library.action: Do this: book thirty minutes with your team. Ask what they'd never admit in a survey.

library.title: Context Is the Whole Job
library.hook: The difference between a useless answer and a good one is usually three sentences of context.
library.message: Who it's for, what it's for, and what constraints apply. Without those the model answers a generic version of your question, which is why the output feels generic.
library.action: Do this: add audience, purpose and constraint to your next prompt. Compare the difference.

library.title: Give It the Bad Examples
library.hook: Showing what wrong looks like works better than describing what right looks like.
library.message: Descriptions are abstract and get interpreted loosely. A rejected example is concrete: the model can see the failure mode and steer away from it in a way adjectives never achieve.
library.action: Do this: paste in one bad example and one good one. Two examples beat a paragraph of instruction.

library.title: Asking for the Reasoning
library.hook: Asking for the reasoning helps sometimes, and is theatre other times.
library.message: On multi-step problems, working through it improves the answer. On recall questions it produces a confident-sounding justification for whatever it was going to say anyway.
library.action: Do this: ask for reasoning on analysis. Don't mistake a rationale for evidence.

library.title: Iterate, Don't Restart
library.hook: When an answer is half right, steer it. Don't start over.
library.message: Rewriting the prompt from scratch throws away the context that produced the good half. Telling it what to keep and what to change usually converges in one or two turns.
library.action: Do this: reply with "keep X, change Y" instead of retyping your request.

library.title: Constraints Beat Adjectives
library.hook: Constraints produce better output than adjectives do.
library.message: "Make it punchy" is interpretation. "Under 200 words, no bullet points, no rhetorical questions, plain language" is instruction. The second gets you something usable on the first attempt.
library.action: Do this: replace every adjective in your prompt with a measurable constraint.

library.title: Reusable Prompt Library
library.hook: The team's best prompts shouldn't live in one person's chat history.
library.message: A shared library saves everyone rediscovering the same technique, and it means a prompt that produces good output can be improved by the next person instead of reinvented.
library.action: Do this: contribute one prompt that works for you. Name yourself as its owner.

library.title: Prompt Versioning
library.hook: A prompt running in production is code, and code regresses.
library.message: When you change wording, or the model updates underneath you, output quality can shift in ways nobody notices until a client does. Untracked prompts have no rollback.
library.action: Do this: version your production prompts and record what changed and why.

library.title: The Follow-Up Question
library.hook: Make it ask you questions before it answers.
library.message: The fastest quality improvement available: tell the model to ask what it needs to know first. It surfaces the assumptions it would otherwise have invented silently.
library.action: Do this: end your prompt with "ask me anything you need before answering."

library.title: Length, Format, Audience
library.hook: Three parameters fix most disappointing output.
library.message: Length, because unspecified means medium and bland. Format, because structure changes what gets included. Audience, because expertise level changes everything from vocabulary to what's left unsaid.
library.action: Do this: specify all three by default. It takes ten extra words.

library.title: Knowing When to Stop Prompting
library.hook: There's a point where prompting again is slower than writing it yourself.
library.message: If you've iterated three times and it's not converging, the task probably needs judgement the model can't supply, or context you can't easily provide. Sunk cost keeps people going.
library.action: Do this: set a three-attempt rule. After that, write it yourself.

library.title: AI for Sales Outreach
library.hook: AI-assisted outreach can be genuinely personal or obviously mechanical.
library.message: The difference is whether you fed it something real about the prospect. Generated personalisation from a job title alone produces the emails everyone deletes and remembers you for.
library.action: Do this: give it one specific, verified detail about the recipient, or don't personalise at all.

library.title: AI in Hiring
library.hook: AI can support hiring. There are steps it must not touch.
library.message: Sorting, ranking or filtering candidates carries legal restrictions in many markets, requires explainability, and is where discrimination claims land. Drafting a job ad is fine; scoring a person is not.
library.action: Do this: check what's permitted before automating any part of a hiring decision.

library.title: AI for Finance Teams
library.hook: Finance teams get real value from AI, right up to the numbers.
library.message: Summarising variance commentary, drafting reports and explaining a policy all work well. Producing, adjusting or reconciling a figure does not, and no output should reach a statement unchecked.
library.action: Do this: let AI write about the numbers. Never let it produce them.

library.title: AI in Legal Review
library.hook: First-pass reading of a contract: useful. Legal advice: no.
library.message: AI can find clauses, flag unusual terms and summarise obligations, which saves real hours. It cannot tell you whether to accept a term, and it is confidently wrong about jurisdiction-specific points.
library.action: Do this: use it to find things faster. Send the actual question to legal.

library.title: AI for Customer Support
library.hook: In support, the model drafts and a human sends. That order matters.
library.message: Draft-and-review keeps speed and keeps accountability. Auto-send removes the one step that catches the reply that's technically correct and completely wrong for this customer.
library.action: Do this: never enable automatic sending on customer-facing replies.

library.title: AI in Engineering
library.hook: Generated code helps most where you're strong and hurts most where you're weak.
library.message: In a language you know, it accelerates you and you catch the errors. In one you don't, it produces plausible code you cannot evaluate, which is how subtle bugs reach production.
library.action: Do this: only accept generated code you could have written and can review.

library.title: AI for Marketing Content
library.hook: Marketing content moves fastest and carries the most public risk.
library.message: Every factual claim needs substantiation, every statistic needs a source, and brand voice needs a human ear. The cost of a wrong claim is not the correction; it's the screenshot.
library.action: Do this: route all external content through the standard review, however small.

library.title: AI in Procurement
library.hook: AI can help you compare proposals. It shouldn't pick the winner.
library.message: Summarising differences, extracting terms and building a comparison grid all save time. Scoring vendors introduces a rationale you didn't construct and can't defend in a challenge.
library.action: Do this: use it to structure the comparison. Make the decision yourself, in writing.

library.title: AI for Executives
library.hook: If a number in your briefing came from AI, ask three questions.
library.message: Where did this figure originally come from? Who verified it? What would change if it were wrong by a factor of two? Confident numbers in decks are how bad decisions get made quickly.
library.action: Do this: ask for the source before you repeat a figure to the board.

library.title: AI for Admin and Scheduling
library.hook: Scheduling, formatting, summarising, reformatting. Low risk, real hours.
library.message: The unglamorous tasks are where AI pays for itself with almost no exposure: no customer data, no external audience, and errors that are immediately visible to you.
library.action: Do this: automate one recurring admin task this week. Start where the risk is nearly zero.

library.title: Credential Leakage in Prompts
library.hook: People paste API keys into chat windows because it's faster. It always surfaces.
library.message: A key in a prompt is a key in a third-party log, potentially in a training set, and definitely outside your control. Rotation is the only remedy, and it's needed immediately.
library.action: Do this: if you've ever pasted a credential, rotate it today and tell security.

library.title: Malicious AI Tools
library.hook: Some AI tools exist specifically to harvest what you paste into them.
library.message: Cloned interfaces, browser extensions imitating known products, and free assistants with no discoverable company behind them. The output is real enough that nobody questions the source.
library.action: Do this: only reach tools through links in the registry, never through search results or ads.

library.title: AI-Written Phishing
library.hook: The old advice about spotting phishing by bad grammar is dead.
library.message: Attackers now produce fluent, contextually accurate messages in any language, referencing real colleagues and real projects. Fluency has stopped being a signal of legitimacy.
library.action: Do this: verify the request, not the writing. Check the sender domain and confirm out of band.

library.title: Social Engineering at Scale
library.hook: The technique didn't change. The economics did.
library.message: Targeted social engineering used to require research time per victim. Now the research and the writing are nearly free, so everyone is worth targeting individually rather than in bulk.
library.action: Do this: assume any approach could be tailored to you specifically. Treat familiarity as normal, not reassuring.

library.title: Poisoned Inputs
library.hook: A document can be written to manipulate the AI that reads it.
library.message: Hidden instructions in a CV, an invoice, or a web page can redirect a summarising model, extract earlier context, or trigger an action in a connected system.
library.action: Do this: never let AI summarise external content in a workflow that can act on the result.

library.title: Data Exfiltration via Chat
library.hook: Chat windows are an exfiltration path that bypasses every control you have.
library.message: No email gateway, no USB policy, no DLP rule on a browser tab. Data leaves in a text box, one paste at a time, and looks like ordinary work.
library.action: Do this: understand that this is monitored, and that the reason is proportionate.

library.title: Model Output as Untrusted Input
library.hook: Never feed generated text into something that executes it.
library.message: Output is untrusted input. Passing it to a shell, a database query, an API call or an eval function is the same class of mistake as trusting user input, with the same consequences.
library.action: Do this: validate and constrain AI output before any system acts on it.

library.title: Third-Party Plugin Review
library.hook: Before a plugin connects to anything internal, someone has to check it.
library.message: Who wrote it, what permissions it requests, where data goes, and whether it's maintained. Plugin ecosystems have weak review, and the install takes one click.
library.action: Do this: route every integration request through review. No exceptions for "it's just a plugin".

library.title: Impersonation of Colleagues
library.hook: The message came from someone you report to. It sounded exactly like them.
library.message: Written, spoken or on video, impersonation is now cheap and convincing. The requests are urgent, plausible, and designed so that verifying feels rude.
library.action: Do this: verify through a channel you initiated. Anyone legitimate will respect it.

library.title: Incident Response for AI Events
library.hook: The first thirty minutes of an AI incident set up everything after it.
library.message: Preserve the conversation, the prompts, the outputs and the logs before anything is deleted. Then contain: disable the integration, revoke the credential, stop the automation.
library.action: Do this: know who you call. Preserve first, investigate second, communicate third.

library.title: Personal Data Definitions
library.hook: Personal data is broader than most people assume.
library.message: Names and emails obviously. Also device identifiers, IP addresses, staff numbers, photographs, voice recordings, location traces, and combinations of otherwise harmless fields that identify one person.
library.action: Do this: when in doubt, assume it's personal data and apply the stricter rule.

library.title: Employee Data in AI Tools
library.hook: Staff information can be used well or turned into surveillance. The line is purpose.
library.message: Aggregate analysis to improve a process is defensible. Individual monitoring without notice is not, and it damages trust far faster than it produces insight.
library.action: Do this: ask whether you'd be comfortable telling the affected staff exactly what you're doing.

library.title: Consent and Notice
library.hook: If AI processes someone's data, they usually have to be told.
library.message: Notice needs to be specific enough to be meaningful: what's processed, why, by which tool, and what choices the person has. Buried in a policy nobody reads doesn't count.
library.action: Do this: check that a notice exists before you start processing, not after.

library.title: Anonymisation Is Harder Than It Looks
library.hook: The dataset had no names in it. It was still re-identifiable.
library.message: Postcode, date of birth and gender identify most people. Add a job title or a rare attribute and anonymisation collapses. Removing the obvious fields is not the same as removing identity.
library.action: Do this: get anonymisation reviewed before treating a dataset as safe to share.

library.title: Subject Access Requests
library.hook: When someone asks for their data, AI systems are in scope.
library.message: That includes prompts mentioning them, generated content about them, transcripts, and anything in a vector index. If you can't search it, you can't respond to the request properly.
library.action: Do this: know where AI-held personal data lives before a request arrives.

library.title: Special Category Data
library.hook: Some categories of data need a different answer, not a stricter one.
library.message: Health, biometrics, religious belief, trade union membership, sexual orientation, political opinion. Processing these usually requires a specific legal basis, not just care and good intentions.
library.action: Do this: if any of these appear in your data, stop and get advice before proceeding.

library.title: Children's Data
library.hook: Data about children carries a higher bar and fewer exceptions.
library.message: Consent rules differ, retention expectations are tighter, profiling is often restricted outright, and regulators treat failures far less forgivingly than they do with adult data.
library.action: Do this: if minors are in scope, treat it as a formal review, never an informal judgement.

library.title: Recording and Transcription Consent
library.hook: Get agreement before the notetaker joins, not after it's transcribing.
library.message: Consent obtained retrospectively isn't consent. For external participants, the obligation is clearer still, and in some jurisdictions recording without it is a criminal matter.
library.action: Do this: announce it at the start and give people a real chance to object.

library.title: AI in Performance Reviews
library.hook: AI can help write a review. It cannot decide the outcome.
library.message: Drafting language from your own notes is legitimate and saves time. Generating an assessment, a rating or a ranking of a person is a decision that requires documented human reasoning.
library.action: Do this: write your judgement first, then use AI to express it clearly.

library.title: Monitoring Staff with AI
library.hook: We monitor some things. We say which, and why, in plain terms.
library.message: Covert monitoring destroys trust permanently and is unlawful in many places. What's monitored, the purpose, retention and who can access it are all published, and staff can ask.
library.action: Do this: read the monitoring notice. Ask if anything in it is unclear.

library.title: Who Owns This Use Case
library.hook: Before a pilot starts, one named person owns it.
library.message: Not a team, not a committee. Someone who can say what it's for, what it may touch, and who is accountable if it goes wrong. Unowned pilots are how shadow systems begin.
library.action: Do this: name the owner in writing before any build or trial begins.

library.title: The AI Register
library.hook: One list of every AI system in use, with an owner and a risk rating.
library.message: If it isn't on the register, we can't govern it, patch it, audit it or turn it off. The register is not bureaucracy; it's the only map we have.
library.action: Do this: check whether your team's tools are listed. Add what's missing.

library.title: Risk Tiering a Use Case
library.hook: Sort the use case before you build it: low, medium, high.
library.message: Low: internal, reversible, no personal data. Medium: affects work products or external content. High: touches people's rights, money, safety, or regulated processes. Controls scale from there.
library.action: Do this: tier the use case in the first conversation, not at the review gate.

library.title: From Pilot to Production
library.hook: Pilots become dependencies quietly. Make the transition deliberate.
library.message: Before production: named owner, documented purpose, logging, evaluation results, a rollback plan, and a support route for when it breaks at an inconvenient time.
library.action: Do this: run the production checklist before people start relying on it, not after.

library.title: Exception Requests
library.hook: If a rule doesn't fit your case, ask for an exception. Don't work around it.
library.message: Documented deviations can be assessed, time-limited and reviewed. Undocumented ones look identical to a violation when someone finds them later, because there's no record of the reasoning.
library.action: Do this: submit the exception request. It's usually faster than the workaround.

library.title: Policy Review Cadence
library.hook: The rules will change, because the technology and the law are both moving.
library.message: Policy is reviewed on a fixed cycle and out of cycle when something material shifts. Changes are announced through one channel so you're not tracking several.
library.action: Do this: know where changes are published. Read them when they land.

library.title: Roles and Responsibilities
library.hook: Four roles, four different jobs. Confusing them is how things fall through.
library.message: Who approves a use case. Who reviews the output. Who monitors it in production. Who answers when a client or regulator asks. Often four different people, rarely written down.
library.action: Do this: name all four for your main AI use case. Fill the gaps.

library.title: Escalation Paths
library.hook: An unclear case shouldn't sit in someone's inbox for a week.
library.message: There's a defined route: your manager first, then the AI governance contact, then legal or security depending on the question. Each step has an expected response time.
library.action: Do this: save the escalation contacts somewhere you can find them under pressure.

library.title: Board-Level Reporting
library.hook: The board doesn't need the tool list. It needs four things.
library.message: Where we're using AI and to what value. What could go wrong and what's controlling it. What incidents occurred. What decisions leadership needs to make this quarter.
library.action: Do this: use the standard template. Resist the urge to add detail nobody will read.

library.title: Decommissioning an AI System
library.hook: Turning an AI system off is a project, not a switch.
library.message: Data has to be retrieved or deleted, integrations disconnected, credentials revoked, users migrated, and records retained for the audit period. Skipping steps leaves live access behind.
library.action: Do this: run the decommissioning checklist. Confirm the deletion, don't assume it.

library.title: Vendor Security Questionnaire
library.hook: Most vendor questionnaires ask questions that don't differentiate anyone.
library.message: The useful ones: where is inference processed, is our data used for training, what's the retention, who are the sub-processors, what's your incident notification time, and can we test it?
library.action: Do this: use the standard questionnaire. Follow up on any answer that's a marketing sentence.

library.title: Reading an AI Vendor's Terms
library.hook: Three clauses in an AI vendor's terms matter more than the price.
library.message: Data use and training rights. Liability and indemnity for output. The provider's right to change the service or terms unilaterally. Everything else is negotiable detail.
library.action: Do this: read those three before anything else. They're usually not near the front.

library.title: Indemnity and Liability
library.hook: When generated output causes harm, someone pays. Check who.
library.message: Most standard AI terms cap liability at a few months of fees and exclude consequential loss, while placing responsibility for output squarely on you. Indemnity for IP claims varies enormously.
library.action: Do this: know the cap before you rely on a tool for client-facing work.

library.title: Data Processing Agreements
library.hook: Before data moves, the agreement has to exist in writing.
library.message: Purpose limits, processing locations, sub-processor rules, security measures, breach notification, deletion on termination, and audit rights. Verbal assurances and website copy are not agreements.
library.action: Do this: confirm the DPA is signed before the first upload, not after the pilot.

library.title: Vendor Lock-In
library.hook: The cost of leaving is decided when you join.
library.message: Proprietary formats, embedded prompts, accumulated fine-tuning, integrations and user habit all raise the exit price. By renewal, the alternative to accepting the increase is a migration project.
library.action: Do this: ask how you'd export everything, before you sign.

library.title: Open Models vs. Hosted Services
library.hook: Hosting it yourself buys control and costs you a team.
library.message: Open models remove data-sharing concerns and per-token pricing, and add responsibility for infrastructure, updates, evaluation, security and support. That trade is right for some workloads and wrong for most.
library.action: Do this: cost the people, not just the compute, before choosing.

library.title: Free Tools, Real Exposure
library.hook: Free tools charge in ways that don't appear on an invoice.
library.message: Data used for training, no confidentiality commitment, no support when it breaks, no notice when it changes, and no contract to point at when something goes wrong.
library.action: Do this: assume free means your data is the payment, unless the terms say otherwise clearly.

library.title: Vendor Incident Notification
library.hook: When a provider has an incident, we need to know quickly.
library.message: Contractual notification periods vary from twenty-four hours to "without undue delay", which means whatever their lawyers decide. Our own regulatory clocks start when the incident happens, not when we hear.
library.action: Do this: check the notification commitment in every AI contract you own.

library.title: Renewal Review
library.hook: Renewals roll over quietly. Review before they do.
library.message: Usage may have collapsed, the tool may have been superseded, terms may have changed mid-term, and the security posture may have shifted after an acquisition.
library.action: Do this: diarise a review sixty days before each renewal date.

library.title: Shadow Procurement
library.hook: Corporate cards are the most common route to unapproved AI.
library.message: A small monthly subscription doesn't trigger procurement, doesn't get a security review, and doesn't appear in the register. It does get company data, and usually admin access to something.
library.action: Do this: check your team's card statements for AI subscriptions nobody reviewed.

library.title: Knowledge Cutoffs
library.hook: The model doesn't know what happened after its training ended.
library.message: It will still answer questions about recent events, confidently, by generating what plausibly might have happened. The absence of knowledge is not visible in the output.
library.action: Do this: for anything recent, use a tool with search enabled and check the sources.

library.title: Context Windows
library.hook: There's a limit to how much it can hold, and it doesn't warn you.
library.message: Paste too much and earlier material gets dropped or compressed. The answer will still arrive fluently, based on a partial reading you weren't told about.
library.action: Do this: for long documents, work section by section and confirm coverage.

library.title: Sycophancy
library.hook: It agrees with you more than it should, and that's a failure mode.
library.message: Push back on a correct answer and it will often fold. State a wrong premise and it will build on it politely. Agreement is not confirmation.
library.action: Do this: test a claim by asking it to argue the opposite, not by asking if you're right.

library.title: Arithmetic and Counting
library.hook: Some tasks are structurally hard for these systems. Counting is one.
library.message: Arithmetic, counting items, sorting precisely, tracking state across a long document, and anything requiring exactness rather than plausibility. They fail quietly and confidently.
library.action: Do this: use a calculator or a script for anything numeric. Don't trust the arithmetic.

library.title: Non-Determinism
library.hook: The same prompt can give a different answer tomorrow.
library.message: Output varies between runs by design. That's fine for drafting and a problem for any process where consistency is the point, including anything auditable.
library.action: Do this: don't build a control that depends on identical output every time.

library.title: Silent Truncation
library.hook: It stopped halfway and the ending looked like an ending.
library.message: Truncation at a token limit often produces a plausible closing sentence rather than an obvious cut. The missing third of the analysis is invisible unless you were counting.
library.action: Do this: check long outputs against your expected structure. Confirm every section exists.

library.title: Wrong Refusals
library.hook: Sometimes "I can't help with that" is the tool, not the policy.
library.message: Models decline things that are entirely legitimate — security work, medical topics, legal questions — because of broad safety tuning. That refusal is not a compliance signal.
library.action: Do this: rephrase once. If it's genuinely permitted work, escalate rather than assuming it's banned.

library.title: Overfitting to the Example
library.hook: Give it one example and you'll get twenty variations of that example.
library.message: Single-shot prompting anchors hard. The model treats your sample as the template rather than the illustration, and diversity collapses across the batch.
library.action: Do this: provide three varied examples, or ask explicitly for structurally different options.

library.title: Language and Locale Gaps
library.hook: Quality drops sharply outside the dominant training languages.
library.message: Reasoning degrades, cultural references misfire, and errors become harder for a reviewer to spot because the fluency stays high. This affects some of our markets much more than others.
library.action: Do this: apply heavier review to output in less-resourced languages, not lighter.

library.title: Benchmarks vs. Your Actual Work
library.hook: Benchmark scores rarely predict how a model performs on your work.
library.message: Public benchmarks measure general capability on public tasks. Your work has private context, house conventions and domain specifics that no leaderboard captures.
library.action: Do this: test on twenty of your own real examples before choosing a tool.

library.title: Retrieval Basics
library.hook: Grounding answers in your documents beats relying on the model's memory.
library.message: Retrieval finds relevant material first, then the model answers from it. That makes answers checkable, current, and traceable to a source you control.
library.action: Do this: prefer tools that show you which document each claim came from.

library.title: Garbage In, Confident Out
library.hook: The system answered from a policy that was superseded two years ago.
library.message: Retrieval quality is bounded by library quality. Outdated, duplicated and draft documents get retrieved with the same confidence as current ones, and the answer looks authoritative.
library.action: Do this: clean the source library before blaming the model.

library.title: Document Access Inheritance
library.hook: An AI search tool sees everything your permissions allow, including what you forgot.
library.message: That over-shared folder, the finance drive you were added to once, the mailbox you have delegate access to. Search makes latent over-permissioning immediately exploitable.
library.action: Do this: review your own access before enabling AI search across it.

library.title: Summarising Long Documents
library.hook: Summarisation reliably loses the same things.
library.message: Caveats, minority views, conditional language, and the one paragraph that contradicts the main argument. What survives is the dominant thread, which is sometimes exactly the wrong takeaway.
library.action: Do this: read the sections a summary skipped, especially anything hedged.

library.title: Meeting Notes You Can Trust
library.hook: Generated meeting notes get the discussion right and the actions wrong.
library.message: Owners get misattributed, tentative suggestions become commitments, and dates mentioned in passing become deadlines. Everyone reads the actions and nobody reads the transcript.
library.action: Do this: confirm every action, owner and date before circulating.

library.title: Version Control for AI Content
library.hook: Six months later, nobody knows which version a human actually checked.
library.message: Without a convention, AI drafts and reviewed documents look identical. That matters when a claim is challenged and you need to show who verified it.
library.action: Do this: mark drafts clearly and record the reviewer in the file, not in a chat.

library.title: Labelling AI-Generated Files
library.hook: Provenance needs to survive the download.
library.message: Once a document leaves your system, a note in the interface is gone. Labelling belongs in the file: metadata, a footer, or a naming convention that travels with it.
library.action: Do this: apply the standard label to any AI-assisted document that leaves the team.

library.title: Knowledge Base Hygiene
library.hook: Your AI answers are only as good as the library behind them.
library.message: Curation is the highest-leverage work in any retrieval deployment: removing superseded documents, resolving contradictions, and marking which source is authoritative.
library.action: Do this: nominate an owner for the source library. Without one it decays within months.

library.title: Contradictory Sources
library.hook: When two of your documents disagree, the model picks one. Silently.
library.message: It won't flag the conflict; it will produce a confident answer from whichever it retrieved. You'll never know the other document existed unless you check.
library.action: Do this: when the answer matters, ask what sources it used and read them.

library.title: Search Isn't Verification
library.hook: A link next to a claim is not verification. It's a pointer.
library.message: Cited sources are frequently real pages that don't support the specific claim attached to them. The URL resolves, the page exists, the sentence isn't in it.
library.action: Do this: open the source and find the actual sentence. Every time.

library.title: Telling a Client You Used AI
library.hook: Telling a client you used AI works better early and plainly.
library.message: One sentence about how it was used and how it was checked. Defensive framing invites suspicion; matter-of-fact framing usually ends the conversation immediately.
library.action: Do this: use the standard wording. Say it before they ask.

library.title: AI Claims in Proposals
library.hook: Don't promise an AI capability you haven't tested on real work.
library.message: Proposals get quoted back during delivery. A capability that worked in a demo and fails on the client's actual data becomes a contractual problem, not a technical one.
library.action: Do this: only claim what you've run on realistic data and can demonstrate.

library.title: Answering: Is This AI-Written?
library.hook: "Was this written by AI?" deserves a straight answer.
library.message: Detectors are unreliable in both directions and penalise non-native writers particularly badly. The defensible answer describes your process and your review, not a detector score.
library.action: Do this: answer honestly about the process. Never rely on a detection tool to settle it.

library.title: Public Statements and Media
library.hook: Only certain people speak publicly about how we use AI.
library.message: Casual comments in interviews, at conferences and on social platforms become quoted positions, sometimes contractual ones. The topic attracts more scrutiny than most.
library.action: Do this: route media and public speaking questions on AI through communications first.

library.title: Regulator and Auditor Questions
library.hook: When a regulator or auditor asks, the answer should already exist.
library.message: The register, the policies, the risk assessments, the evaluation records and the incident log. Assembling these under a deadline produces gaps that look like concealment.
library.action: Do this: keep the evidence pack current. Review it quarterly, not on request.

library.title: Explaining an AI Error to a Client
library.hook: When AI causes a client-facing error, the recovery is a human conversation.
library.message: What went wrong, what you're doing about it, what changes so it doesn't recur. Blaming the tool reads as evasion, because the client contracted with you.
library.action: Do this: lead with ownership and the fix. Explain the mechanism only if asked.

library.title: Internal Announcements
library.hook: How you announce a tool determines whether people adopt it or route around it.
library.message: Say what it's for, what data it may touch, what it replaces, and where to get help. Vague announcements produce shadow usage of something else entirely.
library.action: Do this: use the launch template. Include the "what you may not use it for" section.

library.title: Saying No to a Stakeholder
library.hook: Sometimes the right answer to a stakeholder is no. Say it well.
library.message: Explain the specific risk, offer the closest permitted alternative, and name what would need to change for the answer to become yes. Unexplained refusals get escalated over your head.
library.action: Do this: never decline without offering a route forward.

library.title: Marketing Claims About AI
library.hook: There's a line between positioning and misrepresentation, and it's regulated.
library.message: Describing a rules-based process as AI, overstating autonomy, or implying capability you don't have attracts consumer protection scrutiny in an increasing number of markets.
library.action: Do this: describe what the system actually does. Marketing language still has to be true.

library.title: Supplier and Partner Expectations
library.hook: Our obligations flow to the people who work with our data.
library.message: Suppliers, contractors and partners handling client information are bound by the same restrictions we accepted. That has to be written down, not assumed from a good relationship.
library.action: Do this: include the AI clauses in supplier agreements. Check subcontractors are covered too.

library.title: Baseline Skills for Everyone
library.hook: There's a floor, and everyone stands on it.
library.message: Know what these tools do and don't do. Classify data correctly. Verify before sending. Know when to escalate. Know the reporting route. That's the whole baseline.
library.action: Do this: check yourself against the five. Any gap is training you should ask for.

library.title: Advanced Practitioner Track
library.hook: Heavy use and capable use are not the same thing.
library.message: The advanced level is about evaluating output quality, designing review into a workflow, knowing when not to use the tool, and being able to teach someone else safely.
library.action: Do this: if you use AI daily, take the practitioner assessment. Frequency isn't competence.

library.title: Job Change, Not Job Loss
library.hook: The honest version: tasks change before jobs do.
library.message: Drafting, summarising and first-pass analysis compress. Judgement, relationships, accountability and knowing what question to ask do not. Most roles rebalance rather than disappear, and some get harder.
library.action: Do this: identify which of your tasks are shifting. Invest in the parts that aren't.

library.title: Over-Reliance and Skill Fade
library.hook: The skill you stop practising is the skill you lose.
library.message: If you never draft from scratch, editing gets harder. If you never do the analysis, you lose the instinct for when the analysis is wrong. Both matter for reviewing AI output.
library.action: Do this: keep one task a week that you do entirely yourself.

library.title: Verification Is a Skill
library.hook: Checking output is real work, and it belongs in the estimate.
library.message: Teams promise AI-accelerated delivery and then discover verification takes the time drafting used to. Unbudgeted review is why review gets skipped under deadline.
library.action: Do this: include verification time explicitly when you estimate an AI-assisted task.

library.title: Peer Review Circles
library.hook: The fastest way to improve is to see how a colleague uses the same tool.
library.message: Review circles surface techniques nobody documents and mistakes nobody reports. They also normalise saying "I didn't check that", which is where the value is.
library.action: Do this: swap one AI-assisted piece of work with a colleague this month.

library.title: Measuring Real Time Saved
library.hook: Time saved is only real if you counted the review.
library.message: Drafting dropped from ninety minutes to ten, and checking took forty. That's still a gain, but it isn't the number people quote, and the difference compounds across a business case.
library.action: Do this: measure end to end, including rework and the times it didn't work.

library.title: Cost per Task
library.hook: Cost per task is knowable, and mostly nobody knows it.
library.message: Licence spend divided across actual users, plus usage costs, against the hours genuinely saved. Some heavily promoted use cases cost more than the manual process they replaced.
library.action: Do this: calculate it for your top use case before expanding it.

library.title: Tracking Adoption Honestly
library.hook: Logins are not adoption. Adoption is changed work.
library.message: Seat counts and weekly active users tell you about curiosity. What matters is whether a process runs differently, faster, or with fewer errors than it did before.
library.action: Do this: measure a process outcome, not a usage statistic.

library.title: Quarterly Lessons Learned
library.hook: Near-misses are the cheapest lessons available, and they expire.
library.message: If nobody writes them down within a quarter, the detail is gone and the same mistake recurs somewhere else. Every good card in this library started as somebody's bad afternoon.
library.action: Do this: submit one near-miss this quarter. It doesn't need to be dramatic.

library.title: Your First Prompt
library.hook: Start with a task where you already know the right answer.
library.message: It's the only way to calibrate. Ask something you could grade yourself, see how the output compares, and learn where this tool is strong and where it quietly invents.
library.action: Do this: pick a task from last week. Run it again with AI and compare honestly.

library.title: Where to Get Help
library.hook: You will get stuck. Here's exactly where to go.
library.message: The support channel for how-to questions, your team's champion for workflow questions, security for anything involving data, and governance for "am I allowed to". Response times are published.
library.action: Do this: save the channel now, before you need it in a hurry.

library.title: What You're Allowed to Try
library.hook: There's a sandbox, and you don't need permission to play in it.
library.message: Public information, internal non-sensitive documents, your own drafts, and anything you'd be happy to see on a screen in reception. Experiment freely inside that boundary.
library.action: Do this: spend twenty minutes trying things in the sandbox this week.

library.title: Three Habits to Build Early
library.hook: Three habits, built in the first month, prevent most problems later.
library.message: Verify anything you'll act on. Log anything that matters. Ask when you're unsure rather than deciding alone. Everything else in this library is detail on top of those three.
library.action: Do this: pick the one you're weakest at and practise it deliberately.

library.title: Common Beginner Mistakes
library.hook: Almost everyone makes the same five mistakes in week one.
library.message: Pasting too much. Trusting a confident number. Using a personal account. Accepting the first output. And not telling anyone when something looked wrong.
library.action: Do this: read the list, then notice which one you're about to make.

library.title: Setting Up Your Account
library.hook: Set the account up properly once and you avoid a whole class of problem.
library.message: Sign in through the company identity provider, confirm you're on the enterprise workspace, turn off any training or history setting that's on by default, and check the retention shown.
library.action: Do this: run the setup checklist. It takes five minutes.

library.title: Your First Verified Output
library.hook: Your first real deliverable: produce something, check it properly, record what you found.
library.message: Not a test exercise — actual work. The point is to experience the gap between how good it looked and what verification actually turned up.
library.action: Do this: do it this week and write down the errors you found. Share the count.

library.title: Who Else Is Using This
library.hook: Someone on your floor has already solved the problem you're about to hit.
library.message: The internal directory lists colleagues using AI, what for, and whether they're happy to be asked. It's faster than the documentation and considerably more honest.
library.action: Do this: find one person doing similar work and ask them what didn't work.

library.title: The Thirty-Day Checkpoint
library.hook: By day thirty, you should be able to do five things without help.
library.message: Classify data before submitting it. Write a prompt with context and constraints. Verify output against a source. Know which tools are approved. Know how to report a problem.
library.action: Do this: check yourself against the list. Book help for anything missing.

library.title: Reading Your Own Usage
library.hook: You can see what you've asked. It's worth looking.
library.message: Your own usage history shows patterns you won't notice in the moment: the tasks you rely on it for, the ones you've stopped checking, and anything you pasted that you shouldn't have.
library.action: Do this: review your last two weeks of prompts. Look for data you'd rather hadn't been sent.

library.title: Chats, Projects and Threads
library.hook: One long thread degrades. Start a new one.
library.message: As a conversation grows, earlier context gets compressed or dropped, and unrelated material from earlier bleeds into new answers. Separate work into separate threads deliberately.
library.action: Do this: start a fresh conversation for each distinct task, not each day.

library.title: System Instructions
library.hook: Standing instructions apply before you type anything.
library.message: System or custom instructions set role, tone, constraints and format for every message in a thread. Set once, they save repeating yourself and produce far more consistent output.
library.action: Do this: write standing instructions for your most common task type.

library.title: File Uploads
library.hook: Some file formats are read well. Others get quietly mangled.
library.message: Clean text and simple documents work. Complex spreadsheets, scanned PDFs, multi-tab workbooks and heavily formatted files often lose structure, and the model won't tell you what it missed.
library.action: Do this: for critical documents, ask it to list what it found before you ask it to analyse.

library.title: Web Access On and Off
library.hook: Turning web search on changes what you get, in both directions.
library.message: It brings currency and citations, and it also brings low-quality sources, SEO content and occasional contradictions the model resolves silently in favour of whatever it read last.
library.action: Do this: enable search when currency matters. Then check the sources it used.

library.title: Temperature and Creativity Settings
library.hook: The creativity dial changes reliability, not just style.
library.message: Lower settings produce consistent, conservative, sometimes flat output. Higher settings produce variety and more invention, including inventing facts. Analysis wants low; brainstorming wants high.
library.action: Do this: use the low setting for anything factual. Most people never change it.

library.title: Saved Instructions and Profiles
library.hook: Teach the tool your preferences once instead of every conversation.
library.message: Saved profiles can hold your role, your audience, your house style and the things you always have to correct. It removes the repetition that makes people write lazy prompts.
library.action: Do this: add the three corrections you make most often to your saved instructions.

library.title: Exporting a Conversation
library.hook: Threads disappear. If it matters, get it out.
library.message: Retention policies, workspace changes and accidental deletion all remove conversations. Anything that supports a decision or deliverable needs to live in your document system.
library.action: Do this: export the prompt and output alongside the work product, not in the tool.

library.title: Sharing a Chat With a Colleague
library.hook: Sharing a chat shares more than the answer you meant to send.
library.message: The whole thread travels: the earlier questions, the file you uploaded, the version you rejected, and the aside about a colleague. Recipients see all of it.
library.action: Do this: read the full thread before sharing, or copy just the relevant output.

library.title: Mobile vs. Desktop Use
library.hook: A small screen changes the risk, not just the convenience.
library.message: People skim more, verify less, paste more freely, and are more likely to be on a personal account. Mobile use is where good habits quietly lapse.
library.action: Do this: don't do work on mobile that you'd insist on reviewing on desktop.

library.title: Keyboard Shortcuts and Speed
library.hook: Small mechanics compound across a working week.
library.message: Keyboard shortcuts, saved prompts, quick file attachment and fast thread switching sound trivial and add up to real time, mostly by removing the friction that makes people take shortcuts.
library.action: Do this: learn three shortcuts for the tool you use daily.

library.title: Email Drafting That Sounds Like You
library.hook: Generated email sounds like nobody, unless you give it something to imitate.
library.message: Paste three emails you've actually written and ask it to match the register. The difference between that and a cold draft is the difference between assistance and obvious automation.
library.action: Do this: keep a sample of your own writing handy and feed it in.

library.title: The Difficult Message
library.hook: AI is genuinely useful for finding the words in a hard message.
library.message: It's good at structure and tone under pressure, when you're too close to the situation. It is not good at deciding what the message should say, which is the actual difficulty.
library.action: Do this: decide the content yourself, then use AI on the wording.

library.title: Meeting Invitations and Agendas
library.hook: Agendas and invitations are a small win you should just take.
library.message: Low risk, no sensitive data, immediately checkable, and it removes a task most people do badly. This is the category to automate first.
library.action: Do this: draft your next three meeting agendas with AI. Notice the time saved.

library.title: Chat and Instant Messages
library.hook: A generated chat reply can be efficient or quietly insulting.
library.message: In a channel where people expect a human, an obviously templated response reads as "I didn't think this was worth my time", which is often the opposite of what you meant.
library.action: Do this: use it for information, not for messages that carry a relationship.

library.title: Tone Calibration
library.hook: Formal, neutral, warm, firm — say which one you want.
library.message: Unspecified means the model picks a default that's usually over-friendly and slightly American. Naming the register, and one phrase to avoid, fixes most tone complaints instantly.
library.action: Do this: name the register in every drafting prompt. One word is enough.

library.title: Writing for Non-Native Readers
library.hook: Writing for colleagues in their second language is a real skill.
library.message: Shorter sentences, common vocabulary, no idioms, explicit structure. AI does this well when asked, and produces something condescending when asked badly.
library.action: Do this: ask for plain language at a specified reading level, not "make it simple".

library.title: Bad News in Writing
library.hook: Bad news needs a human rewrite before it goes anywhere.
library.message: Redundancy, rejection, service failure, a mistake that affected someone. Generated versions are fluent, hollow and immediately recognisable, and people remember how the message felt for years.
library.action: Do this: draft with AI if it helps you start. Rewrite it entirely yourself.

library.title: Templates vs. Fresh Drafts
library.hook: Reuse saves time until it becomes a liability.
library.message: The template that no longer reflects the service, the paragraph that was true for a different client, the claim that changed. Reuse propagates errors faster than fresh writing creates them.
library.action: Do this: date your templates and review them on a cycle.

library.title: Signature Moves to Avoid
library.hook: Certain phrasings make output instantly recognisable as generated.
library.message: Overuse of "delve", "landscape" and "in today's fast-paced world", tricolons everywhere, a summary paragraph restating the opening, and relentless positivity. Readers now notice.
library.action: Do this: keep a banned-phrase list in your standing instructions.

library.title: Reply Triage
library.hook: AI can sort your inbox. It shouldn't decide what matters.
library.message: Categorisation and drafting save real time. Automatic prioritisation buries the short, unusual message from someone important that doesn't match any pattern.
library.action: Do this: let it sort and draft. Scan the low-priority pile yourself.

library.title: Outline Before Draft
library.hook: Agree the structure before anyone writes a word.
library.message: Long documents fail structurally, not sententially. Getting the outline right — and reviewed — makes the drafting straightforward and prevents the rewrite that eats the deadline.
library.action: Do this: produce and approve an outline as a separate step, always.

library.title: Section-by-Section Generation
library.hook: Long documents fail as one prompt and succeed as ten.
library.message: Asking for a forty-page report in one go produces even, shallow, repetitive text. Section by section, with the outline as context, produces something with actual depth.
library.action: Do this: generate one section at a time and keep the outline in every prompt.

library.title: Maintaining Consistency Across Chapters
library.hook: Over forty pages, things drift. Terminology, tense, and claims.
library.message: The same concept gets three names, a figure changes between sections, and the recommendation in chapter two contradicts chapter six. Nobody notices until a reader does.
library.action: Do this: run a consistency pass on terms, numbers and recommendations before submission.

library.title: Proposals and Bids
library.hook: In anything you're contractually bound by, some parts must be human-written.
library.message: Scope, commitments, deliverables, timelines and anything describing capability. Generated versions promise more than intended, in language that reads as commitment.
library.action: Do this: write the obligations yourself. Use AI for the surrounding narrative.

library.title: Policy and Procedure Writing
library.hook: Drafting a rule with AI is fine. The authority behind it isn't delegated.
library.message: Generated policy reads plausibly and often imports requirements from other jurisdictions or industries that don't apply to us, while omitting ones that do.
library.action: Do this: have the accountable owner read every line before it's issued.

library.title: Executive Summaries
library.hook: Write the executive summary last, from the finished document.
library.message: Generated from the brief, it summarises what you intended to write. Generated from the actual document, it summarises what you wrote. Those diverge more than you'd expect.
library.action: Do this: produce the summary as the final step, from the final text.

library.title: Case Studies and Client Stories
library.hook: Client stories need approval before they leave the building, however anonymised.
library.message: Sector, size and problem together identify a client to anyone in the market. "A regional bank with a 2023 breach" is not anonymous to their competitors.
library.action: Do this: get written client approval, even for de-identified case studies.

library.title: Technical Documentation
library.hook: Generated documentation goes stale faster than anything else you write.
library.message: It's produced quickly, in volume, describing a system that changes weekly, and nobody owns it. Six months later it's confidently describing behaviour that no longer exists.
library.action: Do this: date every generated doc and assign an owner, or don't create it.

library.title: Citations and Referencing
library.hook: Every reference gets opened. There is no exception to this.
library.message: Not skimmed, not recognised, opened, with the specific claim located in the text. Fabricated and misattributed citations are the single most common failure in AI-assisted writing.
library.action: Do this: check them as you go. Retrofitting the check never happens.

library.title: Knowing the Document Is Done
library.hook: At some point further iteration makes it worse.
library.message: Additional passes smooth out the specific, the surprising and the human, converging on something correct and forgettable. Knowing when to stop is an editorial skill.
library.action: Do this: set a version limit. If v4 isn't better than v2, ship v2.

library.title: Proofreading vs. Rewriting
library.hook: Ask for proofreading and you'll often get a rewrite.
library.message: The model improves what it touches, which means your author's voice quietly becomes its voice. The change is uniform enough that it reads as an improvement until you compare.
library.action: Do this: ask for a list of corrections, not a corrected version.

library.title: Preserving the Author's Voice
library.hook: Editing someone's work without flattening it takes deliberate instruction.
library.message: Tell the model to preserve voice, keep the author's sentence rhythm, and only change what's wrong. Otherwise everyone's writing converges on the same competent neutral.
library.action: Do this: specify "minimum change" in every editing prompt.

library.title: Cutting Length Without Losing Meaning
library.hook: Compression removes the caveats first.
library.message: Ask for half the length and you lose the conditions, the exceptions, and the hedging that made the claim accurate. What remains is shorter, cleaner, and slightly false.
library.action: Do this: after cutting, check that every remaining claim is still qualified correctly.

library.title: Fact-Checking an Existing Draft
library.hook: Use AI to find the claims. Use a human to check them.
library.message: It's very good at extracting every factual assertion in a document into a list. It is not reliable at confirming them, which is the part that requires sources.
library.action: Do this: extract the claim list automatically, then verify manually.

library.title: Structural Critique
library.hook: The most useful editorial question is what's missing.
library.message: Models are better at critique than at generation. Asking what a reader would find unconvincing, or what the document fails to address, produces genuinely useful notes.
library.action: Do this: ask for the three weakest points and the biggest omission.

library.title: Consistency Checking at Scale
library.hook: Checking consistency across a document set is a task humans do badly.
library.message: Job titles, product names, figures, dates and legal entity names drift across a pack of documents. This is exactly the tedious pattern-matching AI handles well.
library.action: Do this: run a cross-document consistency check before any large submission.

library.title: Accepting and Rejecting Suggestions
library.hook: Accepting all suggestions is how errors get in.
library.message: Bulk-accepting edits means accepting changes to meaning alongside changes to grammar. The single wrong "not" removed from a compliance sentence looks like tidying.
library.action: Do this: review edits individually in anything with legal or factual weight.

library.title: Plain Language Rewrites
library.hook: Plain language is not simplified language.
library.message: Good plain-language rewriting keeps the precision and removes the obstruction. Bad rewriting removes the precision, which in a policy or a client letter changes what was promised.
library.action: Do this: check that every rewritten sentence still means exactly what the original did.

library.title: Reviewing Under Time Pressure
library.hook: Under deadline, some corners must not be cut.
library.message: Reference checking, numbers, names, legal wording and anything client-facing. Everything else can be rougher. Deciding this in advance beats deciding it at 11pm.
library.action: Do this: agree your non-negotiables now, while you're not under pressure.

library.title: The Second Reader Rule
library.hook: Some documents need a reader who wasn't the author.
library.message: AI-assisted work has a particular failure mode: the author reviews their own prompt rather than the output, because they know what it was supposed to say.
library.action: Do this: get a second human on anything external, regulated or high value.

library.title: Choosing a Notetaker
library.hook: Not all notetakers are equal, and some join uninvited.
library.message: Approved options have contracts, retention limits and admin controls. Others join through a participant's personal account, record everything, and store it somewhere nobody can audit.
library.action: Do this: check the registry before letting any notetaker into a meeting.

library.title: Announcing the Bot
library.hook: Tell the room before the recording starts. Every time.
library.message: Not in a calendar note nobody read. Verbally, at the start, with a real chance to object. This is a legal requirement in many places and basic courtesy everywhere.
library.action: Do this: make the announcement part of your standard meeting opening.

library.title: Action Items You Can Trust
library.hook: The actions are the part everyone reads and the part AI gets wrong.
library.message: Owners get misassigned, "we should probably" becomes a commitment, and someone thinking out loud acquires a deadline. Errors here propagate into project plans.
library.action: Do this: verify every action, owner and date before the summary goes out.

library.title: External Attendees
library.hook: External attendees haven't consented to anything.
library.message: Clients, suppliers and candidates need to be asked, not informed as the bot joins. Their own policies may prohibit it, and recording anyway can breach your contract with them.
library.action: Do this: ask in advance for external meetings. Have a no-recording fallback ready.

library.title: Sensitive Meetings
library.hook: Some conversations get no notetaker at all.
library.message: Disciplinary and grievance matters, legal advice, M&A, security incidents, personal circumstances, and anything where candour depends on the absence of a transcript.
library.action: Do this: state "no recording" at the start of these. Check nobody's tool joined anyway.

library.title: Summaries for People Who Missed It
library.hook: A summary tells someone what was said, not what was meant.
library.message: The disagreement that was resolved by tone, the thing everyone understood without saying, the joke that set the direction. Summaries flatten meetings into decisions and lose the reasoning.
library.action: Do this: for consequential meetings, add two lines of human context to the summary.

library.title: Transcript Storage
library.hook: Transcripts are records. Treat them like records.
library.message: They contain candid remarks, personal information and commercially sensitive discussion, and they're searchable. Where they live and who can read them is a real decision.
library.action: Do this: know the retention period and access list for your meeting transcripts.

library.title: Real-Time Assistance in Calls
library.hook: Live suggestions during a call can help or visibly distract you.
library.message: Reading a prompt mid-conversation is obvious to everyone watching, and the pause reads as evasion. The value is highest in structured calls and lowest in relationship ones.
library.action: Do this: use real-time assistance in practice before using it with a client.

library.title: Async Collaboration
library.hook: The genuine win: fewer meetings, because the written record is good.
library.message: If summaries and actions are reliable, the update meeting stops being necessary. This is a bigger productivity gain than anything that happens inside a meeting.
library.action: Do this: cancel one recurring status meeting and replace it with a written summary.

library.title: Meeting Reduction
library.hook: AI can bridge time zones better than it can bridge nuance.
library.message: Summarising overnight discussion for a colleague works well. Conveying that a decision was contentious, or that someone was unhappy, does not.
library.action: Do this: add the human context that the transcript can't carry.

library.title: Framing a Research Question
library.hook: A vague research question produces a plausible, useless answer.
library.message: "Tell me about the market" yields a summary of the market in general. Specifying the segment, geography, timeframe, decision and what would change your mind produces something you can act on.
library.action: Do this: state the decision the research supports before you write the question.

library.title: Desk Research Workflow
library.hook: There's an order to desk research, and skipping steps costs more later.
library.message: Search, read primary sources, verify claims, then synthesise. Starting with synthesis produces a confident narrative built on whatever the model already believed.
library.action: Do this: don't ask for conclusions until you've read the sources yourself.

library.title: Source Quality Ranking
library.hook: Not all sources deserve equal weight, and the model treats them equally.
library.message: A regulator's publication, a peer-reviewed paper, a vendor white paper and a content-marketing blog all arrive as citations. The model can't reliably tell you which one to distrust.
library.action: Do this: rank your sources yourself. Discard the aggregators.

library.title: Competitor and Market Scans
library.hook: Landscape scans are fast now. The numbers still need confirming.
library.message: Competitor lists, positioning summaries and feature comparisons come together in minutes. Pricing, headcount, funding and market share figures are frequently outdated or invented.
library.action: Do this: verify every quantitative claim against the company's own published material.

library.title: Literature and Standards Review
library.hook: Use AI to find the standards and papers. Don't trust the paraphrase.
library.message: It's genuinely good at pointing you to the right document, clause or body of work. It is unreliable at telling you what that document says in detail.
library.action: Do this: use it to locate. Read the source to understand.

library.title: Synthesis Across Many Sources
library.hook: Synthesis averages away the disagreement that mattered.
library.message: When sources conflict, the model produces a smooth consensus that no source actually holds. The disagreement was often the most useful finding.
library.action: Do this: ask explicitly where the sources disagree and why.

library.title: Confirmation Bias in Prompting
library.hook: Ask for supporting evidence and you'll get supporting evidence.
library.message: The model is obliging. Framing determines findings more strongly than most people realise, which makes AI research an efficient way to confirm what you already thought.
library.action: Do this: run the opposite prompt too. Ask it to argue you're wrong.

library.title: Estimating and Sizing
library.hook: Generated estimates become anchors, and anchors are hard to shake.
library.message: Once a number is on the page, subsequent discussion adjusts around it rather than questioning it. This is true of human estimates too, but AI produces them faster and more confidently.
library.action: Do this: build your own estimate first. Compare afterwards.

library.title: Recording Your Method
library.hook: Research nobody can reproduce is an opinion with citations.
library.message: Record the questions asked, the tools used, the sources consulted and what you rejected. Six months on, you won't remember, and someone will ask.
library.action: Do this: keep a method note alongside the findings. Half a page is enough.

library.title: When Research Needs a Human Expert
library.hook: Some questions need a specialist, and the model won't tell you which.
library.message: Where a wrong answer is expensive, where the field is fast-moving, where jurisdiction matters, or where the question is about liability. AI gives an answer regardless.
library.action: Do this: identify the specialist-review threshold for your work and respect it.

library.title: Formulas You Didn't Write
library.hook: A generated formula that produces a number is not a correct formula.
library.message: Off-by-one ranges, wrong absolute references, silently excluded rows. The output looks like a number, so it gets used, and the error propagates through the model.
library.action: Do this: test every generated formula against a case you've calculated by hand.

library.title: Cleaning Messy Data
library.hook: Data cleaning is a genuine strength, with one thing to watch.
library.message: Standardising formats, splitting fields and finding duplicates all work well. Silent transformation — dates reinterpreted, leading zeros dropped, values coerced — happens without any warning.
library.action: Do this: compare row counts and spot-check twenty records before and after.

library.title: Uploading a Spreadsheet
library.hook: Uploading a spreadsheet uploads the whole spreadsheet.
library.message: The hidden columns, the other tabs, the pivot cache, the comments, and the sheet from the last client you used this template for. The model reads all of it.
library.action: Do this: copy the relevant range into a clean file before uploading.

library.title: Pivot Logic and Aggregation
library.hook: Aggregation is where a model quietly changes the question.
library.message: It groups by the wrong field, includes rows you'd filtered, or counts distinct values as totals. The output is a plausible number that answers a slightly different question.
library.action: Do this: state your grouping and filters explicitly, then verify one group by hand.

library.title: Charts That Mislead
library.hook: The chart was accurate and it told the wrong story.
library.message: Truncated axes, misleading scales, cherry-picked ranges and inappropriate chart types all arrive without comment. Generated visuals optimise for looking clear, not for being fair.
library.action: Do this: check the axis, the range and the denominator before showing a generated chart.

library.title: Sampling and Spot Checks
library.hook: Decide how much to verify before you start, not after.
library.message: For a generated dataset, sample size depends on consequence. Ten rows for an internal draft, a statistically meaningful sample for anything a decision rests on.
library.action: Do this: define and record your sampling approach as part of the task.

library.title: Statistical Claims
library.hook: Statistical claims need someone who knows statistics.
library.message: Significance, correlation, causation, confidence intervals and sample adequacy are all areas where the model produces confident, standard-sounding language that is often wrong.
library.action: Do this: get statistical claims reviewed before they appear in anything external.

library.title: Reconciliation Work
library.hook: Matching records is fast with AI. Proving the match is the work.
library.message: Fuzzy matching finds candidates efficiently and produces false positives that look right. In a reconciliation, a wrong match is worse than no match.
library.action: Do this: review every matched pair above a materiality threshold.

library.title: Forecasting With AI
library.hook: Forecasting with AI is useful for shape and dangerous for precision.
library.message: It can help you think about drivers, scenarios and sensitivities. The specific numbers it produces carry an air of derivation they haven't earned.
library.action: Do this: use it for scenario structure. Build the numbers in a model you can audit.

library.title: Data Dictionary Discipline
library.hook: Define every field before anyone analyses anything.
library.message: What "active customer" means, which date is the effective date, whether the figure is gross or net. Undefined fields are how two teams produce two different answers.
library.action: Do this: write the data dictionary first. It takes an hour and saves a fortnight.

library.title: From Document to Deck
library.hook: Turning a document into a deck is a rewrite, not a conversion.
