library.message: Prose logic doesn't survive as bullets. What you get is compressed sentences on slides, which is the format everyone complains about and nobody can follow.
library.action: Do this: ask for the argument restructured for spoken delivery, not the text shortened.

library.title: One Idea Per Slide
library.hook: One idea per slide. The model will ignore this unless you insist.
library.message: Left alone it produces dense, evenly balanced slides with four bullets each, because that's what most decks look like. Most decks are bad.
library.action: Do this: state the constraint explicitly and cut anything that needs a second idea.

library.title: Generated Speaker Notes
library.hook: Generated speaker notes are scaffolding, not a script.
library.message: Read aloud, they sound exactly like what they are. As a prompt for what you already know, they're useful and save preparation time.
library.action: Do this: reduce generated notes to three bullet prompts before you present.

library.title: Numbers on Slides
library.hook: Every number that gets projected gets remembered.
library.message: Figures on slides are quoted, screenshotted and repeated long after the presentation. A wrong number in a deck has a much longer life than a wrong number in a document.
library.action: Do this: trace every figure on every slide to a source before you present.

library.title: Client-Facing Decks
library.hook: Client-facing decks go through review, regardless of how quickly they were made.
library.message: Speed of production is not a reason to skip approval, and it's the main reason people do. The review exists for the audience, not for the effort involved.
library.action: Do this: build review time into the deadline you agree, not the one you hope for.

library.title: Diagrams and Flowcharts
library.hook: Generated diagrams help with structure and invent relationships.
library.message: Boxes and arrows appear that reflect a plausible architecture rather than yours. The layout looks authoritative, which stops people checking whether the connections are real.
library.action: Do this: verify every arrow against the actual system before publishing.

library.title: Brand and Template Compliance
library.hook: House style applies to AI-built slides too.
library.message: Fonts, colours, logo placement and the approved template. Generated decks default to something generic, and the inconsistency is more visible than the content.
library.action: Do this: start from the approved template. Never let the tool choose the design.

library.title: Rehearsing With AI
library.hook: Use it to find the question you'd rather not be asked.
library.message: Ask what an informed sceptic would challenge in your deck. It's good at this, and it's less painful to hear from a model than from the room.
library.action: Do this: run your deck through a hostile-questions prompt before presenting.

library.title: Slide Bloat
library.hook: Generation is cheap, which is exactly the problem.
library.message: Decks grow because adding slides costs nothing. The discipline of "what would I cut" disappears, and the audience pays for it in attention.
library.action: Do this: set the slide count before you generate, and hold it.

library.title: Accessibility in Decks
library.hook: Accessibility isn't automatic in generated slides.
library.message: Low-contrast colour pairs, images with no alt text, reading order that jumps, and text baked into pictures. All of it passes visual inspection and fails for some colleagues.
library.action: Do this: run the accessibility checker before you circulate.

library.title: When a Generated Image Is Appropriate
library.hook: Generated imagery is fine for illustration and never for evidence.
library.message: An internal deck header, a concept sketch, a placeholder: appropriate. Anything that could be read as a photograph of something real: not appropriate, in any context.
library.action: Do this: ask whether a viewer might mistake it for a record of reality.

library.title: Rights in Generated Images
library.hook: What you may publish and what you may own are two different questions.
library.message: Most tools grant broad usage rights. Very few give you enforceable ownership, which matters if the image becomes part of your brand or a client deliverable.
library.action: Do this: check the licence before using a generated image in anything commercial.

library.title: Likeness and Real People
library.hook: Never generate a recognisable person without documented consent.
library.message: Colleagues, clients, public figures — likeness rights, personality rights and data protection all apply. The fact that the image is synthetic is not a defence anywhere.
library.action: Do this: use abstract or non-identifiable imagery. If you need a person, use a licensed photo.

library.title: Brand Assets and Logos
library.hook: Generated versions of trademarks are a legal problem, including your own.
library.message: Approximated logos, near-miss brand marks and competitor imagery all create exposure. Your own brand assets exist in an approved library for exactly this reason.
library.action: Do this: never generate a logo. Use the brand asset library.

library.title: Style Imitation
library.hook: Imitating a living artist's identifiable style is a decision with consequences.
library.message: It's contested legally, contentious publicly, and the resemblance is usually obvious to the people who know the work. The reputational cost lands before any legal question.
library.action: Do this: describe the visual qualities you want, not the artist you want to copy.

library.title: Labelling Generated Imagery
library.hook: If it's published externally, it may need to say it's generated.
library.message: Disclosure requirements are expanding across markets and platforms, and some jurisdictions now mandate labelling of synthetic media in specific contexts.
library.action: Do this: apply the standard label to externally published generated imagery.

library.title: Stock Photography vs. Generation
library.hook: Compare stock and generation honestly, not enthusiastically.
library.message: Stock costs money and comes with a clear licence and a real photograph. Generation is instant and free and comes with ambiguous rights and plausible-looking errors.
library.action: Do this: use stock for anything client-facing. Use generation for internal speed.

library.title: Diagrams the Model Gets Wrong
library.hook: The diagram had six fingers, five legs and confident labelling.
library.message: Technical illustrations, anatomical images, machinery, text within images and anything requiring counting are unreliable. Errors are obvious once noticed and easy to miss.
library.action: Do this: have someone who knows the subject look at any technical image.

library.title: Prompting for Images
library.hook: Four elements produce a usable image prompt.
library.message: Subject, composition, style and constraint. Most disappointing results come from specifying only the first, then adding adjectives instead of structure.
library.action: Do this: name all four. Add what you don't want as an explicit exclusion.

library.title: Images in Regulated Material
library.hook: In some material, generated visuals are prohibited outright.
library.message: Regulatory submissions, evidence, incident documentation, clinical or safety material, and anything presented as a record of fact. The prohibition is about provenance, not quality.
library.action: Do this: check before using generated imagery in anything formal.

library.title: Voice Cloning Rules
library.hook: Voice cloning has a narrow permitted use and a wide prohibited one.
library.message: Documented written consent from the person, for a specified purpose, with a defined retention period. Anything else — including a colleague's voice "just for a demo" — is not permitted.
library.action: Do this: get consent in writing before recording anyone for voice synthesis.

library.title: Synthetic Presenters
library.hook: Synthetic presenters are appropriate in some contexts and corrosive in others.
library.message: Training and product explainers, disclosed as synthetic: acceptable. Leadership messages, apologies and anything requiring sincerity: the discovery costs more than the production saved.
library.action: Do this: never use a synthetic presenter for a message that depends on trust.

library.title: Transcription Accuracy
library.hook: Transcripts fail predictably: accents, jargon and crosstalk.
library.message: Domain terminology becomes similar-sounding nonsense, non-native speakers are transcribed worse, and overlapping speech is attributed to whoever was louder.
library.action: Do this: check the sections that matter. Don't circulate a transcript unread.

library.title: Dubbing and Subtitling
library.hook: Dubbing and subtitling at scale works, with one non-negotiable step.
library.message: Machine output is fast and mostly right, and the errors are exactly the ones a non-speaker cannot detect: register, idiom and unintentional offence.
library.action: Do this: budget for native-speaker review on anything published.

library.title: Video Summarisation
library.hook: Sometimes watching it yourself is still faster.
library.message: For a short video, or one where tone and body language carry the meaning, a summary costs more in verification than the viewing time it saved.
library.action: Do this: summarise long recordings. Watch the short and the sensitive ones.

library.title: Audio Deepfake Awareness
library.hook: A voice you recognise is not authentication and hasn't been for a while.
library.message: Seconds of public audio is enough to clone convincingly, including hesitation and accent. Urgency in the request is the design, not a coincidence.
library.action: Do this: verify by calling back on a number you looked up yourself.

library.title: Generated Music and Sound
library.hook: Generated music and sound still need a licence position.
library.message: Training data provenance is contested, platform terms vary, and "AI-generated" is not a licence. For published material, this is a real risk, not a theoretical one.
library.action: Do this: use the licensed library for anything external.

library.title: Recording Retention
library.hook: Audio and video artefacts accumulate and nobody deletes them.
library.message: Recordings of meetings, calls, training sessions and interviews pile up in tools with generous defaults, containing candid conversation and personal information.
library.action: Do this: know the retention period. Delete what has no reason to exist.

library.title: Accessibility Captions
library.hook: Generated captions need a human pass, especially the technical words.
library.message: Auto-captioning is good enough to look finished and wrong often enough to mislead. For colleagues who rely on captions, the errors are not cosmetic.
library.action: Do this: review captions on anything published, particularly names and terminology.

library.title: Training Videos at Scale
library.hook: Producing training content quickly means producing errors quickly.
library.message: Scale amplifies whatever is in the source. A misunderstanding in one module becomes a misunderstanding taught to four hundred people in six languages.
library.action: Do this: get a subject expert to sign off the source content before scaling production.

library.title: Machine Translation Confidence
library.hook: Some language pairs are reliable. Others need review you can't skip.
library.message: Quality tracks the volume of training data. Major European pairs are strong; low-resource languages, technical registers and regional dialects are considerably weaker, with no warning in the output.
library.action: Do this: know which of your languages need mandatory native review.

library.title: Legal and Contractual Translation
library.hook: Contracts, notices and regulatory filings need a certified human translator.
library.message: Legal effect depends on precise wording, and in many jurisdictions a machine translation has no standing. The cost of a certified translation is trivial against a disputed clause.
library.action: Do this: never submit machine-translated legal text. Use it to understand, not to file.

library.title: Terminology Glossaries
library.hook: House terms have to translate the same way every time.
library.message: Product names, role titles, legal entity names and defined contractual terms. Inconsistent translation across documents creates ambiguity that gets read against you.
library.action: Do this: maintain a glossary and supply it with every translation request.

library.title: Cultural Register
library.hook: Politeness and formality are where machine translation embarrasses you.
library.message: Default output is often too casual for markets where register signals respect, or stiffly formal where it signals distance. Both read as carelessness to a native reader.
library.action: Do this: specify the register and the relationship explicitly in the prompt.

library.title: Back-Translation Check
library.hook: Translating it back catches most of what went wrong in the middle.
library.message: Round-tripping through the model reveals dropped clauses, reversed conditions and shifted meaning quickly, without needing a second language yourself.
library.action: Do this: back-translate anything important and read it as a stranger would.

library.title: Right-to-Left and Script Issues
library.hook: Right-to-left scripts break layouts that survived translation perfectly.
library.message: Punctuation lands wrong, mixed-direction text scrambles, numerals and dates render inconsistently, and templates designed left-to-right fall apart in ways the text preview hides.
library.action: Do this: check the rendered document, not the translated string.

library.title: Multilingual Prompting
library.hook: Prompt in your language or the target one? It depends on the task.
library.message: For translation, source-language instruction is usually clearer. For writing natively in another language, prompting in that language often produces more idiomatic output.
library.action: Do this: try both on a sample and keep whichever reads better to a native speaker.

library.title: Marketing Localisation
library.hook: Slogans, humour and claims don't translate; they get rebuilt.
library.message: Wordplay collapses, cultural references misfire, and a claim that's legal in one market is regulated in another. Localisation is a creative and compliance task, not a language task.
library.action: Do this: brief a local reviewer on marketing content before launch, always.

library.title: Interpreting in Live Meetings
library.hook: Live interpretation is useful and occasionally a liability.
library.message: It helps a conversation flow and it will render an ambiguous phrase decisively, in a negotiation, without flagging that it guessed.
library.action: Do this: use a human interpreter for anything contractual or sensitive.

library.title: Documenting Translation Provenance
library.hook: Record what was machine-translated and who reviewed it.
library.message: When a translated document is later disputed, the question is always who checked it. Without a record, the answer is nobody, whatever actually happened.
library.action: Do this: log the translation method and reviewer alongside the document.

library.title: Autocomplete vs. Generation
library.hook: Autocomplete and full generation are different levels of trust.
library.message: Completing a line you were already writing is low risk. Generating a function, a class or a migration from a description is a different activity with different review requirements.
library.action: Do this: apply full review standards whenever you didn't already know what you wanted.

library.title: Reading Before Accepting
library.hook: The habit that separates useful assistance from technical debt is reading it.
library.message: Accepting suggestions unread is fast today and expensive for two years. The code you didn't read is the code nobody can maintain, including you.
library.action: Do this: read every suggestion before accepting. If it's too long to read, it's too long to accept.

library.title: Licensing of Generated Code
library.hook: Suggested code came from somewhere, and that somewhere had a licence.
library.message: Assistants can reproduce substantial fragments of training data. In a product you distribute, a copyleft fragment is a genuine legal problem, not a theoretical one.
library.action: Do this: run licence scanning on repositories using AI assistance.

library.title: Secrets in the Codebase
library.hook: Your assistant reads the repository, including the file you forgot about.
library.message: Config files with real credentials, test fixtures with production data, comments containing internal URLs. All of it becomes context, and context goes to the provider.
library.action: Do this: scan for secrets before enabling an assistant on a repository.

library.title: Dependency Suggestions
library.hook: Suggested packages sometimes don't exist. Attackers know this.
library.message: Models invent plausible package names, and people install them. Attackers register those names and wait. It's a supply chain attack that requires no compromise at all.
library.action: Do this: verify every suggested dependency exists, is maintained, and is the one you meant.

library.title: Generated Tests Are Not Coverage
library.hook: Tests generated from the code can't find the code's wrong assumptions.
library.message: They confirm the implementation does what it does. They will not tell you the requirement was misunderstood, which is where the expensive bugs live.
library.action: Do this: write tests from the requirement. Use AI to expand coverage afterwards.

library.title: Refactoring at Scale
library.hook: Large mechanical refactors are a real strength, in small verifiable steps.
library.message: The failure mode is a single enormous change nobody can review, where one subtle behavioural difference is invisible among four hundred files.
library.action: Do this: break refactors into reviewable commits with tests passing at each step.

library.title: Legacy Code Comprehension
library.hook: Understanding unfamiliar legacy code is where AI genuinely accelerates you.
library.message: Explaining what a function does, mapping call paths and summarising a module cuts onboarding time substantially, and errors are cheap because you're verifying against the code.
library.action: Do this: use it to orient. Confirm the explanation against the actual behaviour.

library.title: Language You Don't Know
library.hook: Generating code in a language you can't review isn't development.
library.message: It compiles, it runs, and you have no ability to assess whether it's secure, idiomatic, or doing something subtly wrong. You've shipped something nobody understands.
library.action: Do this: get a reviewer who knows the language, or don't ship it.

library.title: Commit Hygiene
library.hook: Marking AI-assisted commits lets review be proportionate.
library.message: Reviewers can apply more scrutiny where it's warranted, and the team can measure where assistance helps and where it generates rework.
library.action: Do this: use the agreed commit convention for AI-assisted changes.

library.title: AI in Code Review
library.hook: AI review is a useful first pass and never the approving reviewer.
library.message: It catches style issues, obvious bugs and missing error handling reliably. It misses architectural problems, security context and whether the change should exist at all.
library.action: Do this: let it comment. Keep a human as the required approver.

library.title: Pipeline Automation
library.hook: AI belongs in some parts of a build chain and not others.
library.message: Generating release notes and triaging failures: fine. Making merge decisions, modifying pipeline configuration, or acting on production without approval: not fine.
library.action: Do this: keep AI out of anything that can deploy without a human gate.

library.title: Generated Infrastructure Code
library.hook: Generated infrastructure code provisions real money and real exposure.
library.message: An over-permissive policy, a public bucket or an oversized instance type all look like working configuration. The error is discovered by the bill or the scanner.
library.action: Do this: run policy-as-code checks on every generated template before apply.

library.title: Release Notes and Changelogs
library.hook: Release notes and changelogs: immediate payoff, almost no risk.
library.message: Structured input, factual output, internal audience, and errors are visible to the person who wrote the code. Start automation here.
library.action: Do this: generate your next changelog from the commit history and edit it.

library.title: Incident Postmortems
library.hook: Draft the postmortem timeline with AI. Keep the analysis human.
library.message: Assembling events from logs and messages is tedious and mechanical. Determining cause, contributing factors and what to change requires judgement about your organisation.
library.action: Do this: automate the timeline. Write the conclusions yourself.

library.title: Ticket Grooming
library.hook: Cleaning a backlog with AI risks losing the context inside it.
library.message: Old tickets contain reasoning, constraints and decisions in the comments. Bulk summarisation and closure discards institutional memory that nobody realises they're using.
library.action: Do this: summarise, don't replace. Keep the original text.

library.title: Estimation and Planning
library.hook: A generated estimate anchors the team badly.
library.message: It arrives with no basis, no assumptions and total confidence, and then every subsequent discussion negotiates against it rather than building an estimate from the work.
library.action: Do this: estimate as a team first. Use AI to challenge, not to produce.

library.title: Documentation Debt
library.hook: Catching up on documentation is easy. Keeping it true is the problem.
library.message: Generation solves the backlog in an afternoon and creates a much larger surface of documentation that will silently diverge from the system.
library.action: Do this: only generate docs you've assigned an owner and a review cycle.

library.title: Rollback Readiness
library.hook: Every AI-assisted change needs a tested way back.
library.message: The failure mode is subtle and delayed: something behaves slightly differently under load, three days later. You need to be able to revert without archaeology.
library.action: Do this: confirm the rollback path before merging, not during the incident.

library.title: Production Access for Assistants
library.hook: Some environments are off-limits to AI tooling.
library.message: Production systems holding customer data, regulated environments, and anything where the assistant's context window would include live records. The convenience isn't worth the exposure.
library.action: Do this: check the environment policy before enabling any assistant.

library.title: Test Case Generation
library.hook: AI gives you breadth of test cases. Experience gives you the ones that matter.
library.message: It reliably produces the standard set and misses the specific edge case your system actually fails on, because that case is in your history, not in its training.
library.action: Do this: generate the breadth, then add the three cases you know from experience.

library.title: Exploratory Testing Prompts
library.hook: Use a model to imagine misuse you wouldn't think of.
library.message: Asking how a feature could be abused, misread or gamed produces a genuinely useful list, because it isn't invested in the design working.
library.action: Do this: run an abuse-brainstorm before release. Keep the three most plausible.

library.title: Synthetic Test Data
library.hook: Synthetic test data is safer than a production copy, within limits.
library.message: It removes the personal data problem and it won't reproduce the messy, malformed, historically inconsistent records that break systems in reality.
library.action: Do this: use synthetic data by default, plus a small properly authorised real sample.

library.title: Regression Risk
library.hook: When the model changes, what do you re-test?
library.message: Anything where output feeds a downstream system, anything with a strict format requirement, and anything a customer sees. Model updates are silent regressions waiting to be found.
library.action: Do this: maintain a regression set and run it whenever a version changes.

library.title: Testing Non-Deterministic Output
library.hook: Testing non-deterministic output needs different assertions.
library.message: Exact matching fails constantly. Test for structure, required elements, prohibited content, and semantic similarity against a reference, with a tolerance you've agreed.
library.action: Do this: define pass criteria that survive legitimate variation.

library.title: Acceptance Criteria for AI Features
library.hook: Define "good enough" before the build, not at the demo.
library.message: Without an agreed accuracy threshold and failure behaviour, acceptance becomes a matter of taste, and the loudest opinion in the room decides whether it ships.
library.action: Do this: write measurable acceptance criteria into the ticket.

library.title: Bug Reports From Users
library.hook: Not every complaint about AI behaviour is a bug.
library.message: Variation between runs, refusals, and answers the user disagreed with are often correct behaviour. Triaging these as defects burns engineering time and hides real problems.
library.action: Do this: separate "wrong" from "unexpected" before raising a defect.

library.title: Performance and Latency
library.hook: Users tolerate less latency from AI than you'd think.
library.message: Beyond a few seconds without feedback, people retry, duplicate requests or abandon. The timeout you set determines the cost as much as the model you chose.
library.action: Do this: show progress early. Set timeouts based on observed user behaviour.

library.title: Failure Mode Cataloguing
library.hook: Catalogue how your AI features actually break.
library.message: Every deployment develops signature failures: a format that breaks parsing, an input type that produces nonsense, a prompt pattern that triggers refusal. Written down, they become detectable.
library.action: Do this: log each new failure mode with its signature and a test case.

library.title: Sign-Off Standards
library.hook: Someone signs off an AI feature, against something written down.
library.message: "It seems to work" is not a release criterion. The sign-off needs an evaluation result, a known-limitations list, and a named person accepting it.
library.action: Do this: follow the release standard. Record who approved and on what evidence.

library.title: Pipeline Code From Prompts
library.hook: Generated pipeline code needs validation against known inputs and outputs.
library.message: Transformations that look right and silently drop rows, coerce types or mishandle nulls are the most expensive category of error, because the damage is downstream and delayed.
library.action: Do this: test with a dataset where you know the correct output exactly.

library.title: Schema Inference Errors
library.hook: The model guessed the schema and got it plausibly wrong.
library.message: A numeric-looking identifier parsed as an integer, dates in an ambiguous format, a currency column typed as text. Everything runs; the numbers are wrong.
library.action: Do this: define the schema explicitly rather than letting anything infer it.

library.title: PII in Development Environments
library.hook: Copying production data to test an AI pipeline is not permitted.
library.message: It's the most common shortcut in data work and the one that puts real personal data into environments with weaker controls and broader access.
library.action: Do this: use synthetic or properly masked data. Request authorisation if you genuinely need real records.

library.title: Data Lineage
library.hook: Knowing where a number came from, three systems back, is the whole job.
library.message: When an AI-assisted report is challenged, lineage is the answer. Without it, you're re-deriving the figure under pressure and hoping you get the same one.
library.action: Do this: record source, transformation and destination for anything reported.

library.title: Embedding and Vector Stores
library.hook: When you index your documents, something specific gets stored.
library.message: Chunks of text and their vector representations, in a store with its own access model, retention and backups. It's a copy of your content, and it's often forgotten in data mapping.
library.action: Do this: include vector stores in your data inventory and retention policy.

library.title: Chunking Decisions
library.hook: How you split documents determines what can ever be found.
library.message: Chunk too small and answers lose context; too large and retrieval gets imprecise. Splitting mid-table or mid-clause makes some content permanently unfindable.
library.action: Do this: test retrieval on real questions before finalising your chunking approach.

library.title: Refresh and Staleness
library.hook: Indexes go stale, and the answers stay confident.
library.message: If the refresh job fails quietly, the system keeps answering from last quarter's documents. Nobody notices until someone acts on a superseded policy.
library.action: Do this: monitor index freshness and alert on failed refreshes.

library.title: Access Control at the Index
library.hook: Permissions have to survive the move into the index.
library.message: If everything is embedded into one store queried by one service account, then every user can reach every document, regardless of the permissions on the originals.
library.action: Do this: verify access control at retrieval time, not just at the source.

library.title: Cost of Reprocessing
library.hook: Re-indexing costs more than people budget for.
library.message: Full reprocessing of a large corpus takes real time and real money, and you'll need to do it when you change models, chunking or embedding approach.
library.action: Do this: know the cost and duration of a full re-index before you commit to an architecture.

library.title: Deleting Data From an Index
library.hook: Deleting data from an index has to actually delete it.
library.message: Removing the source document doesn't remove the embedding, the cache, the backup or the copy in a downstream system. Deletion requests cover all of them.
library.action: Do this: test your deletion path end to end, including backups.

library.title: AI-Assisted Ticket Triage
library.hook: AI triage is good at routing and drafting, not at final categorisation.
library.message: Misrouted tickets and wrong categories distort your data and hide trends. The efficiency gain is real; the categorisation needs sampling.
library.action: Do this: audit a sample of AI-categorised tickets weekly.

library.title: Self-Service Knowledge Answers
library.hook: Sometimes a bot answer is better than a ticket. Sometimes it's a delay.
library.message: For documented, stable, low-stakes questions, self-service is genuinely faster. For anything ambiguous or urgent, it adds a frustrating step before the human.
library.action: Do this: measure whether deflected users came back angrier.

library.title: Escalating an AI Answer
library.hook: There's a point where a human must take the ticket.
library.message: Two failed bot attempts, any mention of a security or safety issue, any regulated request, or any sign of distress. These aren't judgement calls in the moment.
library.action: Do this: configure hard escalation triggers, not just confidence thresholds.

library.title: Runbook Generation
library.hook: A generated runbook is a hypothesis until someone runs it.
library.message: It reads correctly, references plausible commands, and contains a step that doesn't work in your environment. The person who finds out is on call at 3am.
library.action: Do this: test every generated procedure in a lab before it enters the runbook.

library.title: Change Requests
library.hook: Change records should say when AI was involved.
library.message: When a change causes an incident, the first question is what changed and how it was produced. Retrofitting that from memory is unreliable and looks evasive.
library.action: Do this: add the AI-assistance field to your change template.

library.title: Asset and Licence Tracking
library.hook: Every AI tool, every seat, every owner, one place.
library.message: Without this you can't tell what you're paying for, who to contact when something breaks, or what to revoke when someone leaves. Licence sprawl in AI is faster than anywhere else.
library.action: Do this: reconcile AI licences against the register quarterly.

library.title: Onboarding and Offboarding
library.hook: AI access is granted and revoked with everything else, or it isn't revoked.
library.message: Leavers with active AI accounts, movers who kept access to a previous team's assistant, contractors whose subscription outlived the engagement.
library.action: Do this: add every AI tool to the joiner-mover-leaver checklist.

library.title: Service Desk Metrics
library.hook: Deflection rate is the wrong headline metric.
library.message: It measures how many people gave up asking, not how many got helped. Resolution quality, repeat contact rate and satisfaction tell you whether it worked.
library.action: Do this: report resolution and repeat-contact alongside any deflection figure.

library.title: User Complaints About AI
library.hook: Complaints about AI behaviour are a signal, not a nuisance.
library.message: Users notice degradation before monitoring does. "It's got worse" is often an accurate report of a model change, a stale index or a prompt regression.
library.action: Do this: capture AI complaints in a single queue and review the pattern weekly.

library.title: Downtime and Fallback
library.hook: Plan for the day the AI service is down.
library.message: If triage, drafting and knowledge search all depend on one provider, an outage stops the desk. Teams that have never worked without it work badly without it.
library.action: Do this: document the manual fallback and practise it once a quarter.

library.title: Alert Triage With AI
library.hook: AI triage handles volume. Humans handle the ones that matter.
library.message: The gain is real on high-volume, low-complexity alerts. The risk is that the interesting alert gets summarised into the same tone as the noise.
library.action: Do this: sample closed-by-AI alerts regularly, especially the low-severity ones.

library.title: Log Summarisation Limits
library.hook: A summary of security logs is not a security conclusion.
library.message: It can tell you what appears in the data. It cannot reliably tell you nothing happened, and "no indicators found" from a summarisation step is not an assurance.
library.action: Do this: never record a negative finding based only on AI summarisation.

library.title: Threat Intelligence Drafting
library.hook: Verify indicators before they reach a blocklist.
library.message: Generated threat intelligence includes plausible-looking indicators that are wrong, outdated, or belong to legitimate infrastructure. Blocking those creates your own outage.
library.action: Do this: validate every indicator against a source before enforcement.

library.title: Detection Rule Writing
library.hook: Generated detection rules need testing against known-good traffic.
library.message: The failure isn't a missed detection; it's a rule that fires on normal behaviour and buries the analyst in false positives until they disable it.
library.action: Do this: test new rules in monitor mode before enforcing.

library.title: Analyst Skill Erosion
library.hook: If the tool always explains the alert, analysts stop learning to.
library.message: Skill development in security comes from working through unfamiliar alerts. Removing that step produces analysts who can operate the tool and not the problem.
library.action: Do this: keep a rotation where analysts investigate without AI assistance.

library.title: AI in Incident Timelines
library.hook: Reconstructing an incident timeline fast is genuinely valuable.
library.message: Correlating logs, tickets and messages into a sequence saves hours during an incident, when hours matter most. Each entry still needs confirming before it becomes the record.
library.action: Do this: use it live for speed. Verify before the report is final.

library.title: Evidence Handling
library.hook: Forensic artefacts don't go into a chat window.
library.message: Chain of custody, admissibility and confidentiality all break the moment evidence is uploaded to a third-party service. This applies to log extracts and memory dumps too.
library.action: Do this: keep evidence in the approved forensic environment. No exceptions.

library.title: False Confidence in Verdicts
library.hook: It called it benign, confidently, and it wasn't.
library.message: Automated verdicts that close an alert are the highest-risk use in security operations, because the failure produces no signal at all. Nobody investigates a closed alert.
library.action: Do this: sample auto-closed alerts. Track how many were wrong.

library.title: Reporting to Clients and Regulators
library.hook: Every finding reported to a client or regulator has a human signature.
library.message: AI-drafted findings contain overstated confidence, invented CVE references and severity ratings that don't match your methodology. Externally, those are your errors.
library.action: Do this: require named human sign-off on every external finding.

library.title: Tabletop Exercise: AI Failure
library.hook: Practise the day the assistant is wrong and everyone believed it.
library.message: The scenario nobody rehearses: the AI summarised an incident incorrectly, decisions were made on it, and the error is discovered four hours in.
library.action: Do this: run this tabletop once. It changes how people read AI output.

library.title: Service Accounts for AI Tools
library.hook: Service accounts for AI tools: named, scoped, and never shared.
library.message: A shared account means you can't attribute an action, revoke access for one system, or tell a human action from an automated one in the logs.
library.action: Do this: give every AI integration its own identity with its own credentials.

library.title: Least Privilege for Assistants
library.hook: Least privilege for an agent means what it needs this week, not what it might need.
library.message: Permissions granted "to avoid problems later" are the ones that turn a misinterpretation into an incident. Agents act faster and more thoroughly than people do.
library.action: Do this: review agent permissions monthly and remove anything unused.

library.title: Delegated Access
library.hook: When an AI acts as you, the log says it was you.
library.message: Delegated access makes attribution impossible after the fact. If something happens under your identity, the burden of explaining it is yours.
library.action: Do this: prefer separate agent identities over delegation wherever possible.

library.title: Token and Key Rotation
library.hook: Credentials issued to AI systems need lifetimes.
library.message: Long-lived keys in integrations are the ones that leak, get committed to repositories, and remain valid for years after the project ended.
library.action: Do this: set expiry on every AI credential and rotate on schedule.

library.title: Biometric and Face Verification
library.hook: Face and voice verification changed when synthesis got cheap.
library.message: Static biometric checks are now defeatable with generated media. Liveness detection matters more than the biometric itself, and some checks should no longer stand alone.
library.action: Do this: don't rely on voice or face alone for high-value authorisation.

library.title: Joiner-Mover-Leaver
library.hook: AI permissions should follow a role change, not accumulate.
library.message: People move teams and keep access to the previous team's assistants, knowledge bases and agents. Accumulated access is invisible until it's exploited.
library.action: Do this: include AI systems in the mover review, not just the leaver one.

library.title: Access Reviews
library.hook: Access reviews have to cover the non-human accounts too.
library.message: Most attestation processes list people. The agents, integrations and service accounts with equal or greater access are frequently missing entirely.
library.action: Do this: include every AI identity in the quarterly access review.

library.title: Consent for Automated Action
library.hook: Decide which actions an agent may take without asking.
library.message: Reading is usually fine. Writing, sending, paying, deleting and anything visible to a customer should require confirmation until you have strong evidence otherwise.
library.action: Do this: default to confirmation for any external or irreversible action.

library.title: Break-Glass Procedures
library.hook: When you need to stop an agent immediately, procedure beats improvisation.
library.message: Revoke the credential, disable the integration, and know who has the authority to do it at 2am without waiting for approval.
library.action: Do this: document the break-glass procedure and name the people who can execute it.

library.title: Non-Human Identity Inventory
library.hook: You almost certainly have more non-human identities than you think.
library.message: Agents, bots, integrations, scripts and connectors, each with credentials, most created for a project that ended. Nobody owns the list.
library.action: Do this: build the inventory. Start with what has API access to production.

library.title: Where the Model Runs
library.hook: Where the model runs changes everything about your obligations.
library.message: Public API, dedicated tenancy, private cloud or on-premise. Each shifts the data protection position, the cost structure and the amount of work you own.
library.action: Do this: know which one you're using for each workload. Don't assume.

library.title: Region and Residency
library.hook: You may need to prove where inference happened, not just choose it.
library.message: Contracts and regulations specify processing locations. Configuration in a console isn't evidence; documentation from the provider is.
library.action: Do this: obtain and file the residency evidence for regulated workloads.

library.title: Network Egress From AI Tools
library.hook: AI tools talk to places. Know where.
library.message: Assistants, extensions and agents make outbound connections that may include your content. Unrestricted egress from a tool with broad read access is a data path.
library.action: Do this: restrict egress to approved endpoints for anything handling internal data.

library.title: Capacity and Rate Limits
library.hook: Rate limits become your problem at the worst moment.
library.message: Quotas are usually generous until a batch job, a demo or a busy month consumes them. The failure mode is a workflow that stops mid-run.
library.action: Do this: know your limits and what your system does when it hits them.

library.title: Cost Controls
library.hook: One misconfigured loop can spend a month's budget overnight.
library.message: Retries without backoff, an agent that re-reads the same context repeatedly, or a batch job with no cap. The bill arrives after the money is gone.
library.action: Do this: set hard spend limits and alerts, not just budgets.

library.title: Caching and Reuse
library.hook: Caching makes answers cheaper and slightly older.
library.message: Reusing responses cuts cost meaningfully for repeated queries, and returns yesterday's answer to today's question. Whether that matters depends entirely on the use case.
library.action: Do this: decide the acceptable staleness per workload, explicitly.

library.title: Availability Expectations
library.hook: Check what uptime your AI dependency actually offers.
library.message: Many AI services carry weaker availability commitments than the systems you've built around them, and remedies are usually service credits rather than anything meaningful.
library.action: Do this: read the SLA before designing a process that can't run without it.

library.title: Disaster Recovery
library.hook: Recovering a service that depends on someone else's model needs a plan.
library.message: Your own backups don't help if the provider is down. The realistic options are a second provider, a degraded mode, or a documented manual process.
library.action: Do this: decide which one you're relying on, before you need it.

library.title: Environment Separation
library.hook: Development, test and production boundaries apply to AI systems too.
library.message: Shared API keys, prompts edited directly in production, and test agents with production access are all common and all remove your ability to change anything safely.
library.action: Do this: separate environments and credentials properly, as you would for any system.

library.title: Edge and Offline Inference
library.hook: Running models locally trades control for maintenance.
library.message: You gain data residency, predictable cost and independence. You inherit patching, scaling, evaluation, monitoring and the expertise to do all of it.
library.action: Do this: only choose local deployment if you have someone to own it permanently.

library.title: Should This Feature Use AI
library.hook: Ask whether the feature needs AI before the roadmap commits.
library.message: Many problems are better solved by rules, search or better defaults, with predictable behaviour and no ongoing evaluation burden. AI should be the answer to a question, not the premise.
library.action: Do this: write down what a non-AI version would look like. Compare honestly.

library.title: Writing AI Feature Requirements
library.hook: Specifying behaviour that isn't deterministic takes a different kind of requirement.
library.message: You can't say "returns X for input Y". You can specify acceptable ranges, prohibited outputs, required structure, fallback behaviour and measured quality thresholds.
library.action: Do this: define the failure behaviour as precisely as the success behaviour.

library.title: User Expectations Management
library.hook: Users assume more capability than the feature has.
library.message: They expect memory, reasoning, current knowledge and reliability, because the interface implies a conversation. Unmanaged, that gap becomes support load and lost trust.
library.action: Do this: state the limits in the interface, at the moment of use.

library.title: Graceful Degradation
library.hook: Design for the answer the model can't give.
library.message: Every AI feature needs a good failure path: a clear message, a manual alternative, and no dead end. Most disappointment comes from the failure case, not the success case.
library.action: Do this: design and test the failure path before the happy path is finished.

library.title: Feedback Loops in Product
library.hook: Thumbs-down is useless unless it reaches someone who can act.
library.message: Feedback widgets collect signals into a table nobody reads. The value is in routing them to the person who owns the prompt or the retrieval library.
library.action: Do this: assign an owner to the feedback queue and review it weekly.

library.title: Pricing AI Features
library.hook: Variable cost per use meets fixed-price expectations.
library.message: AI features cost money every time they're used, and heavy users cost multiples of light ones. Flat pricing on a usage-driven cost is how a successful feature loses money.
library.action: Do this: model cost per active user at three usage levels before pricing.

library.title: Competitive AI Claims
library.hook: Don't match a competitor's claim you haven't verified.
library.message: Marketing claims about AI capability are frequently aspirational. Matching them commits you to delivering something that may not exist anywhere.
library.action: Do this: test the claim before responding to it in your own roadmap.

library.title: Deprecating an AI Feature
library.hook: Removing an AI feature people rely on needs care.
library.message: Users build workflows around it quickly, often in ways you didn't anticipate. Withdrawal without a migration path generates more complaint than the feature generated value.
library.action: Do this: give notice, provide an alternative, and explain the reason.

library.title: Roadmap Under Model Change
library.hook: Your dependency ships breaking improvements.
library.message: Models get better and behave differently, sometimes on short notice, occasionally with deprecation of the version you built on. Roadmaps that assume stability get disrupted.
library.action: Do this: track provider deprecation notices and budget for periodic re-testing.

library.title: Defining Success Before Launch
library.hook: Agree what success looks like while the feature is still a document.
library.message: Post-launch, success becomes whatever the data supports. Defining the metric in advance is the only way to learn anything from the launch.
library.action: Do this: write the success metric and the kill criterion into the spec.

library.title: Designing for Uncertainty
library.hook: Interfaces should show uncertainty honestly.
library.message: Presenting a generated answer with the same visual authority as a database lookup teaches users to trust both equally. Design carries an implicit claim about reliability.
library.action: Do this: distinguish generated content from retrieved fact visually.

library.title: Making Review Easy
library.hook: If checking the output is hard, nobody checks it.
library.message: Review happens when the source is one click away, the change is highlighted, and the comparison is easy. Otherwise verification loses to convenience every time.
library.action: Do this: make the source and the diff visible by default.

library.title: Undo, Edit and Override
library.hook: Every AI action needs a way back.
library.message: Undo, edit and override are not nice-to-haves; they're what makes it safe for a user to try. Without them, people either avoid the feature or accept whatever it produced.
library.action: Do this: ship undo with the feature, not in a later release.

library.title: Disclosure in the Interface
library.hook: Tell users when they're talking to a machine.
library.message: Required in a growing number of jurisdictions and expected nearly everywhere. Discovering it later feels like deception even where the interaction was fine.
library.action: Do this: disclose at the start of the interaction, in plain language.

library.title: Dark Patterns in AI Products
library.hook: Some design choices manufacture trust the system hasn't earned.
library.message: Simulated typing, human names, false confidence indicators and hiding the option to reach a person. These work, which is precisely the problem.
library.action: Do this: don't design for trust. Design for accuracy and let trust follow.

library.title: Onboarding Users to AI Features
library.hook: Teach capability and limits in the same breath.
library.message: Onboarding that only shows what the feature can do produces users who discover the limits through failure, usually at the worst moment.
library.action: Do this: include two examples of what it won't do well in your onboarding.

library.title: Error Messages for AI Failures
library.hook: AI error messages should say what happened, not apologise vaguely.
library.message: "Something went wrong" leaves the user unable to decide whether to retry, rephrase or give up. Say whether it was a limit, a refusal, an outage or a bad input.
library.action: Do this: write specific error messages for the four common failure types.

library.title: Research With Synthetic Users
library.hook: Synthetic users are a rehearsal, not research.
library.message: They generate plausible responses drawn from patterns in text, not from your actual customers' constraints, budgets and habits. Useful for testing a script; useless as evidence.
library.action: Do this: use them to prepare. Never cite them as findings.

library.title: Generated Copy in Interfaces
library.hook: Generated microcopy still carries legal weight.
library.message: Consent language, disclaimers, error text and terms links are all copy, and all reviewed. Generated versions frequently soften or omit required wording.
library.action: Do this: route interface legal text through the same review as any other legal text.

library.title: Accessibility of AI Interactions
library.hook: Accessibility of AI interactions is often an afterthought.
library.message: Streaming responses confuse screen readers, latency breaks navigation expectations, and output structure is inconsistent between runs, which assistive technology handles badly.
library.action: Do this: test AI features with a screen reader before release.

library.title: Analysing Feedback at Scale
library.hook: Themes from thousands of comments, verified against a sample.
library.message: Clustering feedback at scale is a genuine strength. The theme labels and the proportions attached to them need checking against actual comments.
library.action: Do this: read fifty raw comments per theme before quoting a percentage.

library.title: Sentiment Analysis Limits
library.hook: Sentiment analysis misses sarcasm, culture and context.
library.message: "Great, another update" scores positive. Politeness conventions in some languages mask dissatisfaction entirely. The aggregate number is confidently wrong in a consistent direction.
library.action: Do this: use sentiment as a trend signal, never as a measurement.

library.title: Survey Design With AI
library.hook: Generated survey questions carry generated assumptions.
library.message: Leading phrasing, false dichotomies, and options that reflect what the model expects rather than what your customers experience. Bad questions produce data that looks rigorous.
library.action: Do this: have someone who knows the customers review every question.

library.title: Customer Data in Analysis Prompts
library.hook: Aggregate freely. Identify never.
library.message: Analysis across customers is legitimate and valuable. Prompts about a named individual, or that could re-identify one, are a different activity with different rules.
library.action: Do this: strip identifiers before any analysis prompt.

library.title: Interview Synthesis
library.hook: Keep the quotes that contradict the pattern.
library.message: Interview synthesis converges on the majority view and discards the outlier, which is frequently the most informative response in the set.
library.action: Do this: ask specifically for the responses that don't fit the theme.

library.title: Persona Generation
library.hook: Generated personas are scaffolding, not evidence.
library.message: They're useful for structuring a conversation and dangerous when quoted in a decision, because they encode assumptions with the appearance of research.
library.action: Do this: label generated personas as hypotheses. Validate before they influence anything.

library.title: Churn Signals
library.hook: A churn prediction should start a conversation, not a decision.
library.message: Acting automatically on a predicted score — withdrawing service, changing pricing, deprioritising support — punishes customers for a pattern they didn't create.
library.action: Do this: use predictions to prompt human outreach, not automated action.

library.title: Voice of the Customer Reporting
library.hook: Report what customers said, not what the model inferred.
library.message: Voice-of-customer reporting drifts toward interpretation, which then gets quoted as fact in strategy documents. The distinction disappears within two hops.
library.action: Do this: keep verbatim quotes alongside every synthesised finding.

library.title: Bias in Whose Feedback You Have
library.hook: The loudest segment is not the market.
library.message: AI analysis of the feedback you have amplifies whoever complains most, in whichever language and channel you collect from. The silent majority is silent in the data too.
library.action: Do this: check who's missing from the sample before drawing conclusions.

library.title: Acting on Insight Responsibly
library.hook: Some decisions about people need more than a pattern.
library.message: Pricing differentiation, service level allocation and eligibility all become fairness questions the moment they're driven by a model rather than a rule you can explain.
library.action: Do this: get any customer-affecting automated decision reviewed before deployment.

library.title: CRM Data Entry and Enrichment
library.hook: AI can do CRM admin well and pollute the record easily.
library.message: Auto-generated summaries and enrichment save real time, and inaccurate enrichment propagates into segmentation, reporting and forecasting, where nobody questions it.
library.action: Do this: mark AI-populated fields so downstream users know their provenance.

library.title: Lead Scoring With AI
library.hook: Ranking prospects is a decision with fairness implications.
library.message: Lead scoring driven by historical conversion encodes who you sold to before, which may correlate with things you'd rather not systematise.
library.action: Do this: check what your scoring model is actually using as signals.

library.title: Call Notes and Follow-Ups
library.hook: Call notes and follow-ups are the highest-value low-risk win in sales.
library.message: Reps hate writing them, they get written badly or not at all, and the AI version is usually better than what would otherwise exist.
library.action: Do this: automate the notes. Keep the rep's own next-step judgement.

library.title: Proposal Assembly
library.hook: Reused proposal content still has to be true for this client.
library.message: The paragraph that was accurate for a different sector, a different scope or a different year arrives looking finished and gets read as a commitment.
library.action: Do this: check every reused claim against this engagement before sending.

library.title: Pricing Discussions
library.hook: Never let a model state a price or a discount.
library.message: Generated pricing appears in emails and proposals and becomes an offer the client reasonably relied on. This has happened to other companies publicly.
library.action: Do this: keep pricing out of AI-generated client-facing content entirely.

library.title: Competitive Battlecards
library.hook: Battlecards are only useful if the claims are current and sourced.
library.message: Competitor information ages fast, and generated competitive claims are frequently wrong. Repeating a wrong claim to a prospect costs credibility immediately.
library.action: Do this: date every claim and cite the source. Review quarterly.

library.title: Forecast Commentary
library.hook: Forecast commentary explains a number the model didn't produce.
library.message: AI can help articulate why the pipeline moved. It should not generate the pipeline figure, the probability or the close date.
library.action: Do this: produce the numbers in the system. Use AI only for the narrative.

library.title: Client Research Before a Meeting
library.hook: Fast client research is real, once the facts are confirmed.
library.message: Company background, recent news, likely priorities and sensible questions come together in minutes. Names, roles, figures and recent events all need checking.
library.action: Do this: verify anything you plan to say out loud in the meeting.

library.title: Contract Redlines
library.hook: A clean-looking redline is not a reviewed contract.
library.message: AI comparison of terms against a playbook is a useful first pass and misses the interaction between clauses, which is where the risk usually sits.
library.action: Do this: legal reviews every contract, regardless of how the redline was produced.

library.title: Sales Coaching From Call Data
library.hook: Coaching from call recordings needs consent and fairness.
library.message: Automated scoring of conversations affects people's assessments and progression, and the models are trained on patterns that may favour particular speaking styles.
library.action: Do this: publish what's scored, how, and how someone can challenge a score.

library.title: Deflection vs. Frustration
library.hook: Measure whether the bot helped or just delayed the human.
library.message: Deflection looks like success and can be a customer who gave up, complained elsewhere, or came back angrier through a more expensive channel.
library.action: Do this: track repeat contacts and escalation sentiment, not just containment.

library.title: Escalation Triggers
library.hook: Some phrases must reach a person immediately.
library.message: Mentions of harm, legal action, regulatory complaint, bereavement, financial hardship or safety. These are hard triggers, not confidence-threshold decisions.
library.action: Do this: review your escalation trigger list with someone who has handled these calls.

library.title: Agent Assist in Real Time
library.hook: Agent assist should support the human, not script them.
library.message: Suggestions that appear as prompts help. Suggestions that must be followed produce robotic conversations that customers can hear and agents resent.
library.action: Do this: keep suggestions advisory. Measure whether agents actually use them.

library.title: Vulnerable Customers
library.hook: Some customers should not be handled by automation at all.
library.message: Vulnerability indicators — distress, confusion, financial difficulty, bereavement — require a person, and in regulated sectors this is a supervisory expectation, not a preference.
library.action: Do this: know your vulnerability triggers and route them out of automation.

library.title: Quality Monitoring With AI
library.hook: Automated quality scoring has to be fair, visible and appealable.
library.message: People's assessments are affected by it. If they can't see the criteria or challenge a score, it becomes a source of grievance rather than improvement.
library.action: Do this: publish the criteria and provide a real appeal route.

library.title: Knowledge Base as the Bottleneck
library.hook: A support bot is only as good as the article behind it.
library.message: Most bot failures are content failures: the answer doesn't exist, is outdated, or is written for a different audience. Improving the model won't fix that.
library.action: Do this: fix the top twenty missing or outdated articles before tuning anything.

library.title: Multilingual Support
library.hook: Decide which languages you actually support with AI.
library.message: Offering automated support in a language you can't escalate in, or where quality is materially worse, creates a two-tier experience your customers will notice.
library.action: Do this: only enable languages where you have a human escalation path.

library.title: Complaint Handling
library.hook: Regulated complaints require a human response.
library.message: Financial services, healthcare, utilities and telecoms all carry complaint-handling rules that specify timescales, records and human consideration. Automation of the response itself is usually prohibited.
library.action: Do this: route anything identified as a complaint out of automated handling.

library.title: Wrap-Up and Disposition Codes
library.hook: Wrap-up codes are tedious, mechanical and worth automating.
library.message: Agents rush them at the end of a call and the data quality suffers, which corrupts every report built on it. This is a good automation target.
library.action: Do this: automate disposition coding, then audit accuracy monthly.

library.title: Telling the Caller It's a Bot
library.hook: Tell the caller it's a bot. At the start, in every channel.
library.message: Discovering it mid-conversation makes people feel deceived and makes them distrust everything the bot said. Disclosure costs nothing and is increasingly required.
library.action: Do this: state it in the first message, in plain words.

library.title: Volume Is Not Strategy
library.hook: Generating more content rarely fixes the underlying problem.
library.message: If the content wasn't working, more of it won't work either. Volume without a point of view produces exactly what the market is already saturated with.
library.action: Do this: fix the positioning before you scale the production.

library.title: Factual Claims in Campaigns
library.hook: Every claim in a campaign needs substantiation on file.
library.message: Performance figures, comparisons, superlatives and customer outcomes. Generated copy produces these enthusiastically, and advertising regulators do not care where the sentence came from.
library.action: Do this: keep the evidence file. If you can't substantiate it, cut it.

library.title: SEO and Generated Content
library.hook: Search engines have views on generated content, and they change.
library.message: Mass-produced low-value content has been targeted repeatedly by ranking updates. Useful content that happens to be AI-assisted is treated differently from content produced to fill a page.
library.action: Do this: optimise for whether a human finds it useful. That's the durable strategy.

library.title: Personalisation Boundaries
library.hook: Personalisation has a line, and crossing it feels invasive.
library.message: Using data the customer knows you have is fine. Using inferred attributes, or data from a context they didn't expect, produces the message that makes people uncomfortable.
library.action: Do this: only personalise on data the customer would expect you to hold.

library.title: A/B Testing Generated Variants
library.hook: Cheap variants don't lower the bar for statistical discipline.
library.message: Generating forty subject lines is easy. Declaring a winner on two hundred impressions is the same mistake it always was, just faster.
library.action: Do this: set sample size and duration before the test starts.

library.title: Email Deliverability
library.hook: Volume and templating patterns get you filtered.
library.message: Deliverability depends on sending behaviour and engagement, not content quality. A sudden increase in similar-looking messages is exactly the pattern spam filters look for.
library.action: Do this: scale send volume gradually and monitor deliverability metrics.

library.title: Regulated Advertising
library.hook: Some sectors need compliance sign-off on every word.
library.message: Financial promotions, health claims, and anything regulated carry pre-approval requirements that apply regardless of how quickly the copy was produced.
library.action: Do this: know which of your content types require sign-off. Build the time in.

library.title: Content Calendars
library.hook: Production capacity is no longer the constraint. Plan differently.
library.message: Content calendars built around how much a team could write are the wrong shape. The new constraints are review capacity, distribution and audience attention.
library.action: Do this: plan against review capacity, not writing capacity.

library.title: Attribution and Reporting
library.hook: Generated analysis of your marketing numbers still needs tying out.
library.message: Attribution summaries and performance narratives read authoritatively and are built on whatever was in the export, including the rows you meant to filter.
library.action: Do this: verify the totals against the source platform before reporting.

library.title: Brand Voice Guidelines for AI
library.hook: Your tools are configured against a brand voice document. Check which one.
library.message: If the guidelines are outdated, generic or contradictory, every piece of generated content inherits that. This document does more work now than it ever did.
library.action: Do this: review the brand voice document with AI generation in mind.

library.title: Approval Before Posting
library.hook: Nothing generated goes live unreviewed, however small.
library.message: Social posts are the shortest content with the widest reach and the fastest amplification of a mistake. Length is not a proxy for risk.
library.action: Do this: keep human approval on every post, including replies.

library.title: Responding to Comments
library.hook: Speed matters in social replies. Tone-deaf speed is worse than silence.
library.message: Generated responses to complaints, especially emotional ones, read as dismissive. The screenshot of an inappropriate automated reply travels further than the original complaint.
library.action: Do this: never automate replies to negative or emotional posts.

library.title: Trend-Jacking Risk
library.hook: The model doesn't know why that topic is sensitive today.
library.message: Trend participation requires context the model lacks: what happened this morning, who's involved, and why joining in would be inappropriate.
library.action: Do this: have a human confirm the context before engaging with any trend.

library.title: Employee Advocacy Posts
library.hook: Staff posting about our AI use needs a clear line.
library.message: Well-meaning posts reveal internal capability, client work and tooling decisions. Most people don't realise which of those is sensitive.
library.action: Do this: publish what staff may and may not say publicly about our AI work.

library.title: Generated Imagery in Social
library.hook: Generated imagery on social needs three checks.
library.message: Rights to use it, disclosure where required, and a plausibility check for the errors that make a brand look careless. Social audiences spot generated images quickly.
library.action: Do this: run all three before posting. Assume it will be scrutinised.

library.title: Community Management at Scale
library.hook: Automated community management can read as contempt.
library.message: Members notice generated replies immediately in a space built on participation. The efficiency gain costs the thing the community was for.
library.action: Do this: use automation for logistics. Keep human voices in the conversation.

library.title: Impersonation of Our Brand
library.hook: Someone will clone your brand with AI. Plan the response.
library.message: Fake accounts, generated executive videos and cloned support channels are cheap to produce and effective. Detection and takedown need to be somebody's job.
library.action: Do this: monitor for impersonation and know your takedown route per platform.

library.title: Comment Moderation
library.hook: Automated moderation decisions need an appeal path.
library.message: False removals affect real people and real customers, and generated moderation is confidently wrong about context, satire and reclaimed language.
library.action: Do this: provide a human review route for every automated removal.

library.title: Influencer and Partner Content
library.hook: Disclosure obligations extend to people you pay.
library.message: Influencers, partners and agencies producing AI-generated content on your behalf create your exposure, under advertising rules that hold the brand responsible.
library.action: Do this: put AI disclosure requirements in every content agreement.

library.title: Archiving Social Output
library.hook: Keep a record of what was published and who approved it.
library.message: Social content disappears from feeds and reappears in screenshots. When a post is questioned months later, the approval trail is the only defence.
library.action: Do this: archive posts with their approver. Automate it if you can.

library.title: Holding Statements
library.hook: Holding statements get drafted fast and approved before release.
library.message: AI genuinely helps under time pressure, producing a structured first draft in minutes. The approval step is what stops a fast statement becoming a worse problem.
library.action: Do this: pre-draft holding statements for your top three scenarios now.

library.title: An AI Incident Becomes News
library.hook: Plan the communications for an AI failure before you have one.
library.message: Who speaks, what's said in the first hour, what's promised, and what's deliberately not said yet. Improvised AI-incident communications go badly with striking consistency.
library.action: Do this: write the plan. Include the version where the failure was preventable.

library.title: Journalist Questions About AI
library.hook: Journalists will ask how you use AI and how you govern it.
library.message: Vague answers read as evasion; over-specific ones create commitments. Prepared, honest, non-technical answers are the only good option.
library.action: Do this: agree the standard answers with communications and legal now.

library.title: Misinformation About Us
library.hook: Generated misinformation about your organisation is cheap to produce.
library.message: Fake statements, fabricated quotes and synthetic executive videos. Response speed matters more than perfect wording, because the first hours determine reach.
library.action: Do this: know who can authorise a rapid correction outside working hours.

library.title: Executive Statements
library.hook: Nothing attributed to a named person goes out unreviewed by that person.
library.message: Generated quotes in press releases, forewords and posts put words in someone's mouth. Even when accurate in substance, they damage trust when discovered.
library.action: Do this: get personal sign-off on every attributed statement.

library.title: Crisis Simulation
library.hook: Rehearse the crisis where the AI system caused it.
library.message: Most crisis exercises assume an external attacker. The harder scenario is an internal system that produced wrong output at scale, and nobody noticed for a week.
library.action: Do this: run this scenario in your next exercise.

library.title: Internal Communications First
library.hook: Staff hear it from us before they read it elsewhere.
library.message: Internal communication that lags external reporting produces speculation, leaks and a workforce learning about their employer from the news.
library.action: Do this: brief staff first, with something honest, even if it's incomplete.

library.title: Monitoring and Listening Tools
library.hook: AI-summarised media monitoring still needs the source read.
library.message: Sentiment scoring and volume summaries miss the one influential piece that shifts a narrative, and mischaracterise nuanced coverage as neutral.
library.action: Do this: read the top five items yourself, whatever the summary says.

library.title: Apologising Well
library.hook: A generated apology sounds like an apology and lands like a form letter.
library.message: Apologies need specificity about what happened, acknowledgement of the effect on the person, and a concrete change. Generated versions supply none of those.
library.action: Do this: write apologies yourself. Use AI only to check clarity.

library.title: Post-Crisis Review
library.hook: Post-crisis review should change policy, not just messaging.
library.message: The comfortable conclusion is that communication could have been faster. The useful one is why the failure was possible and what control was missing.
library.action: Do this: produce at least one policy or control change from every review.

library.title: Job Descriptions
library.hook: Job descriptions get better and more exclusionary at the same time.
library.message: Generated versions default to inflated requirements, gendered language and unnecessary credentials, all of which shrink your candidate pool invisibly.
library.action: Do this: check every generated job ad for unnecessary requirements and coded language.

library.title: CV Screening Constraints
library.hook: Automated CV filtering is restricted in more places than people realise.
library.message: Several jurisdictions require notice, bias auditing, human involvement or all three. Some prohibit specific inferences outright. Vendor claims of compliance are not sufficient.
library.action: Do this: confirm the legal position for every market you hire in.

library.title: Interview Questions
library.hook: Generated interview questions need review for relevance and fairness.
library.message: They drift toward generic behavioural prompts and occasionally toward questions that are unlawful to ask in some jurisdictions.
library.action: Do this: review the question set with HR before it's used, not after.

library.title: Candidate Communication
library.hook: Candidate messages should be read by a person before sending.
library.message: Rejections and offers are the most memorable communications your organisation sends. A generated rejection that misnames the role or the candidate is remembered for years.
library.action: Do this: read every candidate message before it goes. No bulk sending.

library.title: Policy and Handbook Drafting
library.hook: Draft internal rules with AI. Approve them without it.
library.message: Generated policy imports requirements from other jurisdictions and industries, and states them with confidence. The accountable owner has to read every line.
library.action: Do this: treat generated policy as a starting draft, never a final one.

library.title: Grievance and Investigation
library.hook: Grievance and investigation processes are not places for AI assistance.
library.message: Confidentiality, fairness and the appearance of fairness all matter, and AI involvement in an investigation record is a challenge waiting to be made.
library.action: Do this: keep these processes entirely manual and documented.

library.title: Workforce Analytics
library.hook: There's a line between workforce insight and individual scrutiny.
library.message: Aggregate patterns can improve how work is organised. Individual-level analysis of productivity, communication or sentiment damages trust faster than it produces value.
library.action: Do this: set a minimum group size for any workforce analytics output.

library.title: Compensation Analysis
library.hook: Pay decisions need documented human reasoning.
library.message: Generated compensation analysis can inform, and cannot decide. Pay discrimination claims turn on the reasoning, and "the model suggested it" is not reasoning.
library.action: Do this: record the human rationale for every pay decision, separately from any analysis.

library.title: Employee Queries and HR Bots
library.hook: An HR bot can answer some questions and must not answer others.
library.message: Policy lookups, process steps and form locations: fine. Anything about someone's specific situation, entitlement, health or dispute: a person.
library.action: Do this: define the boundary explicitly and test what happens at the edges.

library.title: AI in the Employment Contract
library.hook: Staff should know what they agreed to about AI when they joined.
library.message: Monitoring, tool use, data handling and consequences for misuse. If this only exists in a policy nobody read, it won't hold up and it isn't fair.
library.action: Do this: cover AI expectations explicitly in onboarding, not just in the contract.

library.title: Designing a Course With AI
library.hook: AI gives you course structure. A human supplies the expertise.
library.message: Generated curricula are well-organised and generic, missing the specific mistakes your people actually make, which is where the learning value is.
library.action: Do this: build the structure with AI. Fill it with your own incidents and examples.

library.title: Generated Assessments
