library.hook: Generated assessment questions get people scored on wrong answers.
library.message: Ambiguous phrasing, multiple defensible options and occasionally an incorrect answer key. Learners lose trust in the whole programme after one bad question.
library.action: Do this: have a subject expert review every question before anyone is scored.

library.title: Personalised Learning Paths
library.hook: Adaptive learning needs data you may not be comfortable collecting.
library.message: Personalised paths depend on tracking individual performance, and that record becomes visible in ways learners didn't anticipate.
library.action: Do this: be explicit about what's tracked and who can see it.

library.title: Role-Play Practice
library.hook: Rehearsing difficult conversations with AI actually works.
library.message: A patient, unlimited practice partner for negotiation, feedback, escalation and objection handling. Low risk, and people improve measurably.
library.action: Do this: use role-play practice before your next difficult conversation.

library.title: Knowledge Retention
library.hook: Completion is not learning. Measure behaviour.
library.message: Attendance and completion rates measure compliance with a process. What matters is whether people classify data correctly and verify output afterwards.
library.action: Do this: measure a behaviour, before and after, not a completion rate.

library.title: Micro-Learning Delivery
library.hook: Small cards in the channel people already use beat a course nobody opens.
library.message: Delivery matters as much as content. Two minutes in the flow of work, repeated, outperforms an hour that gets rescheduled twice and skipped.
library.action: Do this: send one card a week rather than one course a year.

library.title: Training the Trainers
library.hook: Anyone teaching AI use internally should demonstrate capability first.
library.message: Enthusiasm is not qualification. An internal trainer who doesn't understand the failure modes will teach confidence rather than judgement.
library.action: Do this: require the practitioner assessment before someone teaches.

library.title: Certification and Renewal
library.hook: A licence has a lifetime, and renewal means something.
library.message: Practice changes, tools change and rules change. A permanent certification issued once tells you nothing about current competence.
library.action: Do this: set the renewal period and what renewal requires. Enforce it.

library.title: Learning From Incidents
library.hook: Every good card in this library started as somebody's bad afternoon.
library.message: Real incidents, de-identified, are the most effective teaching material available, and they expire quickly if nobody writes them down.
library.action: Do this: turn your last near-miss into a card. Nobody needs to know it was you.

library.title: Measuring Programme Impact
library.hook: Link the programme to fewer incidents, not more completions.
library.message: If AI education is working, verification failures fall, shadow tool use falls, and reported near-misses rise before they fall. Those are the numbers to report.
library.action: Do this: report incident trends alongside participation. Only one of them matters.

library.title: Invoice Processing
library.hook: High-volume invoice extraction works, with sampling behind it.
library.message: Accuracy is high and not perfect, and the errors cluster in unusual formats and handwritten fields. Without sampling, you learn about them from a supplier.
library.action: Do this: sample a fixed percentage weekly and track the error rate over time.

library.title: Expense Review
library.hook: Flagging an expense anomaly is fine. Making the accusation is not.
library.message: Automated flags carry an implication about a named person. The flag starts a review; a human decides what it means and how it's raised.
library.action: Do this: never let an automated flag reach the employee directly.

library.title: Month-End Close
library.hook: At month end, some steps stay manual for a reason.
library.message: Journal approval, reconciliation sign-off and anything constituting a key control. Automating the control that exists to catch errors defeats the control.
library.action: Do this: map which close steps are controls. Keep those human.

library.title: Management Commentary
library.hook: Draft the commentary around numbers you produced yourself.
library.message: AI writes variance narrative well when given the actual figures. It invents plausible explanations when the figures are ambiguous or missing.
library.action: Do this: supply the numbers and the drivers. Never let it infer either.

library.title: Budget Modelling
library.hook: Every generated assumption in a model needs writing down and challenging.
library.message: Growth rates, attrition, seasonality and cost inflation arrive embedded in the output, unlabelled. Six months later nobody can say where they came from.
library.action: Do this: list assumptions separately from the model. Have someone challenge each one.

library.title: Payment Instructions
library.hook: No AI system initiates or alters a payment. Ever.
library.message: This is the clearest line in finance. Payment instructions are the highest-value target for manipulation, and AI in the path creates an attack surface with no compensating benefit.
library.action: Do this: verify that no automation in your process can modify payment details.

library.title: Fraud Pattern Detection
library.hook: A fraud signal starts an investigation. It doesn't conclude one.
library.message: Pattern detection is genuinely useful and produces false positives that, treated as findings, damage relationships with customers and colleagues who did nothing wrong.
library.action: Do this: require human investigation before any action on a fraud flag.

library.title: Financial Data in Prompts
library.hook: Pre-release financial results are the most sensitive data we hold.
library.message: Market-moving information in a third-party tool is a securities issue, not just a confidentiality one, and the exposure window is before publication.
library.action: Do this: no unpublished financial data in any AI tool, under any circumstances.

library.title: Audit Requests
library.hook: Auditors will ask how AI was involved in financial processes.
library.message: The answer needs to be documented in advance: which processes, what the tool does, what controls surround it, and what evidence exists that they operate.
library.action: Do this: document AI involvement in your process narratives now.

library.title: Cost Allocation for AI Spend
library.hook: Charge AI spend back so the value is visible.
library.message: Central budgets hide which teams generate cost and which generate return. Allocation forces the conversation about whether a use case is worth what it costs.
library.action: Do this: allocate AI cost to the team that uses it.

library.title: Auditing an AI Process
library.hook: For a control to be testable, evidence has to exist while it operates.
library.message: Retrospective reconstruction of what an AI process did, from memory and screenshots, satisfies nobody. The logging decision is an audit decision.
library.action: Do this: design the evidence at the same time as the control.

library.title: Sampling AI Output
library.hook: Sampling AI output needs a method an auditor would accept.
library.message: Convenience samples of whatever's easy to check aren't evidence. Size, selection basis and the definition of an exception all need to be set in advance.
library.action: Do this: document your sampling approach before you start sampling.

library.title: Segregation of Duties
library.hook: One person plus one agent is still one person.
library.message: Segregation of duties breaks when someone uses an automation to perform the second step. The control assumed two humans with independent judgement.
library.action: Do this: check whether any agent in your process performs a segregated duty.

library.title: Control Design for Automation
library.hook: Controls around agents come in three kinds.
library.message: Preventive: permission limits and approval gates. Detective: logging, monitoring and sampling. Corrective: kill switches and rollback. Most deployments have only the first, weakly.
library.action: Do this: identify which of the three you're missing for your main automation.

library.title: Evidence Retention
library.hook: Prompts, outputs and approvals are audit evidence. Keep them.
library.message: If the process is auditable, the AI artefacts are part of the record and need the same retention as everything else in the process.
library.action: Do this: store AI artefacts in the record system, not in chat history.

library.title: Testing Agent Behaviour
library.hook: Deliberately feed an agent edge cases and see what it does.
library.message: Malformed input, contradictory instructions, empty fields and boundary values. This is how you learn the failure behaviour before a customer does.
library.action: Do this: build an edge-case test set and run it before and after every change.

library.title: Findings and Remediation
library.hook: AI control gaps need tracking to closure like any other finding.
library.message: They're easy to accept as "known limitations" and leave open indefinitely, because the remediation usually involves changing how people work.
library.action: Do this: give every AI finding an owner and a date. Track it in the normal process.

library.title: Management Assertions
library.hook: When leadership attests to AI controls, they're signing something specific.
library.message: That the register is complete, the controls operate, the incidents are reported, and the evidence exists. Each of those needs a basis.
library.action: Do this: make sure whoever signs has seen the evidence, not just the summary.

library.title: Auditing the Prompt Library
library.hook: Production prompts should be reviewed like production code.
library.message: They determine system behaviour, they change, and an unreviewed change can alter output for every user with no code deployment and no record.
library.action: Do this: put prompt changes through the same review and approval as code.

library.title: Reporting to the Audit Committee
library.hook: Explain AI risk to the audit committee without jargon or reassurance.
library.message: What we use, what could go wrong, what's controlling it, what happened this quarter, and what we're not yet good at. The last one is the valuable part.
library.action: Do this: include the honest weakness. Committees notice when reports are only positive.

library.title: AI on the Risk Register
library.hook: Named risks, named owners, current ratings. Not a paragraph about AI.
library.message: "AI risk" as a single register entry is unmanageable. Decomposed into data leakage, output error, dependency failure and misuse, it becomes something you can control.
library.action: Do this: split your AI risk entry into specific, ownable risks.

library.title: Likelihood and Impact for AI Risk
library.hook: Scoring a risk that fails in unfamiliar ways is genuinely hard.
library.message: Likelihood estimates for AI failure modes have little historical basis, and impact is often reputational rather than financial, which resists scoring.
library.action: Do this: use scenarios rather than scores where the numbers would be invented.

library.title: Concentration Risk
library.hook: One provider serving every workflow is a concentration risk.
library.message: Efficient until there's an outage, a price change, a policy shift or a contract dispute. Then it's every workflow at once.
library.action: Do this: map how many critical processes depend on your primary provider.

library.title: Third-Party Dependency Risk
library.hook: Map who you'd lose if a vendor disappeared tomorrow.
library.message: Not just the direct provider — the model behind it, the cloud behind that, and the tools your suppliers use to serve you. Dependencies are deeper than the contract shows.
library.action: Do this: trace the chain for your two most critical AI dependencies.

library.title: Reputational Risk
library.hook: The failure that costs trust rather than money is the harder one.
library.message: A wrong client deliverable, an inappropriate automated message, a discovered undisclosed use. These don't appear in financial impact models and cost more.
library.action: Do this: assess reputational scenarios explicitly. They're rarely the same as the financial ones.

library.title: Risk Appetite Statements
library.hook: Risk appetite for AI should be written down and specific.
library.message: "We take a cautious approach" is not an appetite statement. Which use cases are acceptable, at what risk tier, with what controls, is.
library.action: Do this: express appetite per risk tier, so the answer isn't reinvented each time.

library.title: Emerging Risk Scanning
library.hook: Emerging risk scanning needs to be somebody's standing job.
library.message: The landscape shifts monthly: new capabilities, new attack techniques, new regulation, new precedent. Reviewed annually, your risk assessment is always a year stale.
library.action: Do this: assign the scanning role and set a quarterly review.

library.title: Insurance and Coverage
library.hook: Check what your insurance actually covers for AI incidents.
library.message: Cyber policies frequently exclude errors in professional output, and professional indemnity policies may exclude automated decision-making. The gap is often exactly where the risk is.
library.action: Do this: ask your broker specifically about AI-related exclusions.

library.title: Business Continuity
library.hook: Could you operate for a week without your primary AI provider?
library.message: Teams that adopted AI enthusiastically often can't answer this, because the manual process was quietly abandoned and nobody documented it.
library.action: Do this: identify the processes with no manual fallback. Write one for the critical ones.

library.title: Aggregating AI Risk Upward
library.hook: Many small use cases aggregate into one board-level exposure.
library.message: Individually each is low risk. Collectively they represent a dependency, a data footprint and a control burden that no single assessment captured.
library.action: Do this: report the aggregate position, not a list of individually acceptable items.

library.title: ISO/IEC 42001 in Plain Terms
library.hook: ISO/IEC 42001 in plain terms: govern the AI you use, provably.
library.message: It asks for policy, roles, risk assessment, impact assessment, lifecycle controls, monitoring and improvement — the same management-system shape as other standards, applied to AI.
library.action: Do this: read the clause list once. It's less alien than it sounds.

library.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
library.hook: The NIST framework's four functions map to real activities.
library.message: Govern: who decides and who's accountable. Map: what you have and its context. Measure: evaluation and monitoring. Manage: prioritising and responding. It's a checklist, not a philosophy.
library.action: Do this: place your current activities into the four functions. The gaps are visible immediately.

library.title: ISO/IEC 27001 Overlap
library.hook: If you have ISO 27001, you already have some of this.
library.message: Access control, supplier management, incident response, asset management and awareness all extend to AI. The genuine gaps are impact assessment, evaluation and output quality.
library.action: Do this: map your existing controls first. Only build what's actually missing.

library.title: Mapping One Framework to Another
library.hook: Mapping frameworks to each other avoids doing the work twice.
library.message: Most requirements overlap substantially. One control, evidenced once, can satisfy several standards if the mapping is documented.
library.action: Do this: build the mapping table before you build duplicate controls.

library.title: Evidence for Certification
library.hook: An assessor will ask for specific evidence. Know where it lives.
library.message: Policies with approval dates, the register, risk and impact assessments, evaluation results, training records, incident logs and management review minutes.
library.action: Do this: assemble the evidence pack now. Find the gaps before an assessor does.

library.title: Statement of Applicability
library.hook: The statement of applicability is where you justify exclusions.
library.message: Excluding a control is legitimate and requires reasoning that survives challenge. "Not applicable" without explanation is the most commonly raised finding.
library.action: Do this: write the justification for every exclusion, in a sentence that stands alone.

library.title: Internal Audit Against a Standard
library.hook: Run the audit yourself before the certification body does.
library.message: Internal audit against the standard finds the gaps while you can still fix them quietly, and it tells you whether people can actually describe the controls.
library.action: Do this: schedule an internal audit at least three months before certification.

library.title: Continuous Improvement
library.hook: A management system that only wakes up before audits isn't one.
library.message: Continuous improvement means changes arising from incidents, monitoring and review actually happening between audits. Assessors look for this specifically.
library.action: Do this: keep a log of improvements made outside the audit cycle.

library.title: Sector-Specific Standards
library.hook: Some clients bring their own standards, and they're contractual.
library.message: Sector frameworks, client security requirements and regulatory expectations can exceed the general standards, and they're usually discovered during delivery.
library.action: Do this: check client-specific AI requirements at contract stage, not at delivery.

library.title: Choosing What to Certify
library.hook: Certification serves the business or it serves the brochure.
library.message: It's worth real cost if clients require it, if it unlocks markets, or if it forces discipline you need. It's expensive theatre otherwise.
library.action: Do this: name the specific commercial reason before committing to certification.

library.title: AI Clauses to Request
library.hook: Some AI clauses are worth negotiating into supplier agreements.
library.message: No training on our data, defined processing locations, sub-processor notification, incident notification timescales, deletion on termination, and the right to test.
library.action: Do this: use the standard clause set. Negotiate the ones that matter most first.

library.title: AI Clauses Clients Ask For
library.hook: Clients now ask us to commit to specific AI terms.
library.message: Disclosure of AI use, restrictions on tools, data handling commitments and sometimes a right to audit. Agreeing these casually creates obligations delivery teams don't know about.
library.action: Do this: check that delivery can actually meet any AI clause before signing it.

library.title: Obligation Extraction
library.hook: Extracting obligations across a contract set is useful and needs verification.
library.message: AI finds commitments quickly across hundreds of documents, and it misses conditional language and misattributes obligations between parties.
library.action: Do this: verify every extracted obligation against the clause it came from.

library.title: Contract Summarisation Limits
library.hook: A summary is never the operative document.
library.message: People start working from the summary within a week, and the summary omits the condition, the exception and the notice requirement. The contract is the contract.
library.action: Do this: keep the clause reference next to every summarised obligation.

library.title: Non-Disclosure Agreements
library.hook: Check whether the NDA permits putting their data in a tool at all.
library.message: Many NDAs restrict disclosure to named parties or require prior consent for subcontractors. A third-party AI service is a disclosure, whatever the intention.
library.action: Do this: read the disclosure clause before uploading counterparty material.

library.title: Subcontractor Flow-Down
library.hook: AI obligations have to flow down to subcontractors.
library.message: Your commitment to a client is worthless if the people actually doing the work are using whatever they like. This is where most breaches of AI clauses will originate.
library.action: Do this: include the flow-down clause and check it's been passed on.

library.title: Renewal and Change Notices
library.hook: Vendor terms change mid-contract, and the notice is an email.
library.message: Data use policies, retention and acceptable use get updated unilaterally under most standard terms. What you agreed to may not be what applies today.
library.action: Do this: diarise a terms review for each major AI vendor annually.

library.title: Termination and Data Return
library.hook: Getting your data back and proving theirs is deleted are separate tasks.
library.message: Export formats may be unusable, and deletion confirmations are often assertions rather than evidence. Both need to be agreed before termination, ideally before signature.
library.action: Do this: request the deletion certificate and test the export format early.

library.title: Standard Positions Library
library.hook: Approved fallback language stops everyone negotiating from scratch.
library.message: Without a standard positions library, each deal reinvents the AI clauses, inconsistently, and the concessions accumulate across the portfolio invisibly.
library.action: Do this: use the library. Escalate anything that requires going outside it.

library.title: Escalating a Contract Question
library.hook: There's a point where you stop reading and call legal.
library.message: Ambiguous liability language, unfamiliar jurisdiction, anything about IP ownership, and any clause you'd have to explain to a delivery team. Reading further doesn't help.
library.action: Do this: escalate early. Legal would rather see it before signature.

library.title: Copyright in Generated Text
library.hook: Protection for purely machine-generated text is limited in many places.
library.message: Human authorship requirements mean output with no meaningful human contribution may not be protectable, which matters if you intend to license or enforce it.
library.action: Do this: document the human contribution where ownership matters commercially.

library.title: Substantial Similarity
library.hook: Generated content sometimes resembles a protected work too closely.
library.message: Models can reproduce substantial portions of training data, particularly for well-known text, code and imagery. Similarity is judged on the output, not the process.
library.action: Do this: check distinctive generated content against likely sources before publishing.

library.title: Trade Secrets and Prompts
library.hook: Disclosing a trade secret to a third-party tool can end its secret status.
library.message: Secrecy depends on reasonable steps to keep it secret. Uploading it to a service that may retain or train on it undermines exactly that argument.
library.action: Do this: keep genuine trade secrets out of external tools entirely.

library.title: Patents and AI-Assisted Invention
library.hook: Inventorship questions affect whether you can file at all.
library.message: Most patent offices require a human inventor. Where AI made a material contribution, the position on filing and on who is named is unsettled and jurisdiction-specific.
library.action: Do this: record human contribution contemporaneously in any inventive work.

library.title: Open Source Licence Contamination
library.hook: Copyleft code reaches your product through a suggestion, not a decision.
library.message: Nobody chose to include GPL code. An assistant reproduced a fragment, someone accepted it, and the obligation attached to your distributed product.
library.action: Do this: run licence scanning on any repository using AI assistance.

library.title: Client-Owned Materials
library.hook: What you may do with a client's material is defined by the contract.
library.message: Using client documents to improve your own tools, prompts or knowledge base usually exceeds what was granted, even where the output is anonymised.
library.action: Do this: check the permitted use before client material enters any tool or index.

library.title: Our IP in Someone Else's Tool
library.hook: Free tools are where our IP quietly leaves.
library.message: Staff using personal accounts to work on proprietary material transfer it to a service with training rights and no confidentiality commitment. It's the most common leak we have.
library.action: Do this: make the enterprise tools easy enough that nobody needs a workaround.

library.title: Attribution Obligations
library.hook: Attribution obligations survive generation.
library.message: Content derived from openly licensed material may carry attribution or share-alike requirements. The model won't tell you, and the obligation attaches anyway.
library.action: Do this: check licences on any source material you supply as input.

library.title: Enforcing Against Generated Copies
library.hook: When someone clones our material with AI, options are limited but real.
library.message: Copyright in the original still applies, platform takedown routes exist, and trademark protection is often stronger than copyright for brand material.
library.action: Do this: report suspected copies through the standard route rather than responding directly.

library.title: Recording Provenance
library.hook: Where ownership matters, document the human contribution as you go.
library.message: Reconstructing who wrote what, months later, is unconvincing. Contemporaneous records of human creative input are what support the claim.
library.action: Do this: keep a brief record of human authorship on commercially significant work.

library.title: Why the Rules Differ by Market
library.hook: One product, several regimes, no single compliant answer.
library.message: What's permitted varies by market, and by sector within a market. A global policy set to the strictest requirement is usually simpler than managing variants.
library.action: Do this: know which markets your use case touches before designing the controls.

library.title: Risk-Based Regulation
library.hook: Risk-based regulation explains why the same tool is treated differently.
library.message: The regulation attaches to the use, not the technology. The same model is unregulated for drafting an email and heavily regulated for screening a job application.
library.action: Do this: describe the use case precisely. The classification follows from it.

library.title: Prohibited Practices
library.hook: Some practices are prohibited outright in some jurisdictions.
library.message: Certain forms of biometric categorisation, emotion inference in workplaces and education, social scoring, and manipulative systems. These aren't risk-managed; they're banned.
library.action: Do this: check the prohibited list before designing anything involving people's characteristics.

library.title: Transparency Obligations
library.hook: In a growing number of contexts, the law requires you to say it's AI.
library.message: Chatbots, synthetic media, automated decisions affecting individuals, and AI-generated content in certain sectors. Requirements differ, and they're expanding.
library.action: Do this: check disclosure requirements per market before launch.

library.title: High-Risk Classification
library.hook: Working out whether you're in a high-risk tier is a specific exercise.
library.message: It depends on the domain, the effect on people, and whether the output is decisive. Guessing usually produces the wrong answer in the comfortable direction.
library.action: Do this: run the classification formally and record the reasoning.

library.title: Sectoral Regulators
library.hook: Sector regulators have views, and they're often ahead of general AI law.
library.message: Financial, healthcare, legal, education and telecoms regulators have all issued AI guidance that applies to us before any general regime does.
library.action: Do this: check your sector regulator's guidance, not just the general legislation.

library.title: Horizon Scanning
library.hook: Regulatory change needs a standing process, not an annual panic.
library.message: Consultations, guidance, enforcement actions and precedent all shift what's expected, continuously. Someone has to be watching on purpose.
library.action: Do this: assign the horizon-scanning role and set a quarterly summary.

library.title: Documentation the Law Expects
library.hook: The documentation has to exist before the inquiry, not after.
library.message: Risk assessments, impact assessments, evaluation records and human oversight evidence produced retrospectively look exactly like what they are.
library.action: Do this: create the documentation at design time. It's much cheaper then.

library.title: Cross-Border Service Delivery
library.hook: Serving a client abroad means operating under rules that aren't ours.
library.message: The client's jurisdiction, their regulator and their contractual requirements may all impose AI restrictions that our own policies don't contemplate.
library.action: Do this: check the client's regulatory position at engagement scoping.

library.title: Getting Regulatory Advice
library.hook: There's a point where internal interpretation stops being enough.
library.message: Novel use cases, prohibited-practice questions, cross-border processing and anything where a wrong answer means enforcement. Confidence is not the same as certainty.
library.action: Do this: get external advice on the questions where being wrong is expensive.

library.title: What Red Teaming an AI Means
library.hook: Red teaming an AI system tests behaviour, not just infrastructure.
library.message: The question isn't whether the server is secure; it's whether the system can be made to say, reveal or do something it shouldn't, by an ordinary user with a keyboard.
library.action: Do this: include behavioural testing in your assessment scope.

library.title: Jailbreak Testing
library.hook: Try to make your own deployment misbehave. Someone else will.
library.message: Role-play framings, hypothetical wrappers, encoded instructions and persistence across turns. If you haven't tried, you don't know what your system does under pressure.
library.action: Do this: spend an hour trying to break your own deployment. Write down what worked.

library.title: Prompt Injection Testing
library.hook: Test what happens when the documents your system reads are hostile.
library.message: A CV with hidden instructions, a support ticket containing a directive, a web page crafted to redirect a summariser. This is the most under-tested risk in most deployments.
library.action: Do this: add injected content to your test corpus deliberately.

library.title: Data Leakage Probes
library.hook: Probe whether the system reveals what it shouldn't.
library.message: Ask it about other users, other documents, its own instructions and data outside your permissions. Leakage is usually discovered by a curious user, not a test.
library.action: Do this: include extraction attempts in every assessment.

library.title: Bias and Fairness Testing
library.hook: Bias testing needs structure, or it's just anecdote.
library.message: The same request varied systematically across names, locations, genders and other attributes, with results recorded and compared. Ad-hoc probing finds nothing reliable.
library.action: Do this: use a structured probe set and keep the results for comparison over time.

library.title: Abuse Case Development
library.hook: Imagine the malicious user, not just the confused one.
library.message: Abuse cases are different from edge cases: someone deliberately extracting data, generating prohibited content, or using your system to attack a third party.
library.action: Do this: write three abuse cases per feature and test them.

library.title: Independent Assurance
library.hook: External assurance is worth the cost in specific circumstances.
library.message: When clients require it, when the use case is high risk, when internal capability is thin, or when independence itself is the point.
library.action: Do this: name the reason before commissioning. Otherwise it's an expensive report.

library.title: Findings Triage
library.hook: Behavioural flaws need severity ratings too.
library.message: "The model can be persuaded to produce inappropriate content" needs a severity, an owner and a date, in the same tracker as technical vulnerabilities.
library.action: Do this: use one findings process for behavioural and technical issues.

library.title: Retesting After Changes
library.hook: When the model or prompt changes, some tests have to run again.
library.message: Safety behaviour, output format, refusal boundaries and anything a customer sees. Assurance results have a shelf life measured in model versions.
library.action: Do this: define your re-test trigger and set. Automate what you can.

library.title: Publishing Assurance Results
library.hook: Decide what you publish about your own assurance results.
library.message: Internally, everything. To clients, a summary that's honest about limitations. Publicly, carefully — findings can be a roadmap for someone else.
library.action: Do this: agree the disclosure position before the first assessment.

library.title: Building a Golden Set
library.hook: A hundred examples with known-correct answers, maintained. That's the asset.
library.message: Everything else in evaluation depends on having a golden set. It's tedious to build, it dates quickly, and there's no substitute.
library.action: Do this: build fifty examples this month from real work. Assign someone to maintain them.

library.title: Choosing Metrics That Matter
library.hook: Choose metrics that reflect the actual job.
library.message: Accuracy on a benchmark, usefulness to the user, harm avoided and cost per task all pull differently. Optimising one silently sacrifices another.
library.action: Do this: pick two metrics and state which one wins when they conflict.

library.title: Human Evaluation Protocols
library.hook: Human evaluation needs a protocol, or reviewers disagree with themselves.
library.message: Clear criteria, worked examples of each score, and an inter-rater check. Without those, scores measure the reviewer more than the output.
library.action: Do this: calibrate reviewers on ten shared examples before scoring anything.

library.title: Comparing Two Models
library.hook: Compare two models on your work, not on a leaderboard.
library.message: Same prompts, same golden set, same scoring, blind if possible. Vendor comparisons are constructed to show a difference that may not exist in your context.
library.action: Do this: run a blind comparison on twenty of your real tasks.

library.title: Evaluating Retrieval Quality
library.hook: In retrieval systems, judge the retrieval before you judge the answer.
library.message: If the right document wasn't found, the answer was never going to be right, and tuning the prompt won't fix it. These are separate failures.
library.action: Do this: measure retrieval accuracy separately from answer quality.

library.title: Cost-Quality Curves
library.hook: A cheaper model is often good enough for the task.
library.message: Many workflows use the most capable model by default, for tasks where a smaller one performs identically at a fraction of the cost and latency.
library.action: Do this: test the cheaper option on your golden set before assuming you need the best.

library.title: Regression Suites
library.hook: Regression suites catch what nobody would notice.
library.message: Quality loss from a model update, a prompt edit or an index change is gradual and invisible in daily use, until a customer identifies it for you.
library.action: Do this: run the suite on a schedule, not just on change.

library.title: Evaluating Agents
library.hook: Evaluating an agent means judging a sequence, not an answer.
library.message: Did it take reasonable actions, in a sensible order, stopping when it should, without side effects? A correct final answer can follow a dangerous path.
library.action: Do this: evaluate the trajectory, including what it touched along the way.

library.title: Statistical Confidence
library.hook: Two examples is not a difference. Twenty might not be either.
library.message: Non-deterministic output means small samples show apparent differences that vanish on repetition. Most informal model comparisons are noise.
library.action: Do this: run enough examples that the difference survives repetition.

library.title: Documenting an Evaluation
library.hook: Write the evaluation down so someone else could challenge it.
library.message: Method, dataset, scoring criteria, results and limitations. An undocumented evaluation is an opinion that happened to involve data.
library.action: Do this: use the standard template. Include what the evaluation didn't test.

library.title: What to Log
library.hook: Decide what to log before you need it.
library.message: Inputs, outputs, model version, prompt version, user, timestamp and any human decision. With privacy applied, so the log itself isn't a new exposure.
library.action: Do this: agree the logging schema at design time, not after the first incident.

library.title: Detecting Quality Drift
library.hook: Quality drifts before users complain, and the complaint is late.
library.message: By the time people report degradation, they've been working around it for weeks and some output has already gone out.
library.action: Do this: run a small automated quality check on live traffic daily.

library.title: Usage Anomalies
library.hook: A usage spike means adoption or abuse. Find out which.
library.message: Sudden volume from one account, unusual hours, or a pattern of near-identical requests all warrant a look before you celebrate the adoption numbers.
library.action: Do this: alert on anomalous usage patterns, not just on total volume.

library.title: User Feedback Signals
library.hook: Turn thumbs-down into an investigable queue.
library.message: Raw feedback counts tell you nothing actionable. Feedback with the prompt, output and context attached, routed to an owner, tells you what to fix.
library.action: Do this: capture the context with the rating, or don't bother capturing the rating.

library.title: Alerting on AI Failures
library.hook: Decide what pages someone and what doesn't.
library.message: Error rate, latency, cost and safety-relevant events warrant alerting. Quality metrics usually warrant a weekly review instead, or people learn to ignore the alerts.
library.action: Do this: set thresholds deliberately. Review anything that fires more than weekly.

library.title: Sampling Live Output
library.hook: Review a slice of real output every week.
library.message: Automated metrics miss what a person notices immediately: tone drift, subtle inaccuracy, and answers that are technically fine and unhelpful.
library.action: Do this: put twenty real outputs in front of a human every week.

library.title: Traceability End to End
library.hook: Reconstructing why the system said that, months later, requires design.
library.message: Model version, prompt version, retrieved documents and configuration all have to be recorded at the time. None of it is recoverable afterwards.
library.action: Do this: log the full context of a response, not just the response.

library.title: Privacy in Monitoring
library.hook: Observing behaviour shouldn't build a surveillance archive.
library.message: Detailed logs of what people asked, over years, is a dataset with its own risks and its own legal obligations, particularly where prompts contain personal content.
library.action: Do this: apply retention and access controls to monitoring data specifically.

library.title: Dashboards People Actually Read
library.hook: Three numbers that change decisions beat thirty that don't.
library.message: Most AI dashboards are built for reassurance and get ignored within a month. The useful ones answer questions someone actually asks.
library.action: Do this: ask the owner what decision each metric supports. Delete the rest.

library.title: Closing the Loop
library.hook: Monitoring only pays off if findings change something.
library.message: Detected drift, recurring complaints and identified failure modes need to feed back into prompts, retrieval libraries, training and policy. Otherwise it's observation.
library.action: Do this: assign an owner for acting on monitoring findings, not just producing them.

library.title: Meaningful Human Review
library.hook: Meaningful review means the reviewer could realistically have said no.
library.message: Time to read it, information to judge it, authority to reject it, and no penalty for doing so. Remove any one and it's a rubber stamp with a name attached.
library.action: Do this: check all four conditions exist for your review steps.

library.title: Automation Bias
library.hook: People agree with the machine more than they should.
library.message: Automation bias is well documented: reviewers accept confident output they would have questioned from a colleague, particularly under time pressure.
library.action: Do this: review the output before you see the system's confidence rating.

library.title: Designing the Checkpoint
library.hook: Put the checkpoint where the reviewer can still change the outcome.
library.message: After the send, the payment or the publication, review is only useful for learning. The gate belongs before the irreversible step.
library.action: Do this: map the irreversible point in your process. Put the human immediately before it.

library.title: Reviewer Workload
library.hook: Too many items to check means nothing gets checked.
library.message: A reviewer with four hundred daily approvals is a formality. Oversight capacity is a real constraint that determines how much automation is safe.
library.action: Do this: calculate realistic review capacity before setting automation volume.

library.title: Authority to Override
library.hook: Saying no to the system has to be genuinely supported.
library.message: If overriding creates extra work, requires justification nobody else provides, or gets questioned by a manager, people stop doing it within weeks.
library.action: Do this: make the override path as easy as acceptance, and never penalise it.

library.title: Oversight of Agents
library.hook: Watching a process that runs faster than you can read needs different oversight.
library.message: Real-time review is impossible for agents. Oversight becomes approval gates on consequential actions, plus sampling and monitoring afterwards.
library.action: Do this: define which actions need pre-approval. Sample the rest.

library.title: Two-Person Rules
library.hook: Some actions need a second human regardless of confidence.
library.message: Payments above a threshold, permission changes, external communications to certain parties, and anything irreversible affecting a customer.
library.action: Do this: list your two-person actions and check no automation bypasses them.

library.title: Explaining a Decision to the Affected Person
library.hook: When someone asks why, you need an answer that isn't "the system decided".
library.message: People affected by a decision are increasingly entitled to an explanation, and always entitled to it in practice if they're a client.
library.action: Do this: confirm you could explain any automated decision in plain language.

library.title: Measuring Override Rates
library.hook: If nobody ever overrides, oversight isn't happening.
library.message: An override rate of zero means reviewers are approving by default. It's the clearest available signal that a control has become a formality.
library.action: Do this: track override rates. Investigate any process sitting at zero.

library.title: Fatigue and Rotation
library.hook: Review quality decays over months, not days.
library.message: Reviewers habituate. The hundredth similar output gets less attention than the tenth, and the error that slips through is usually late in a shift or a project.
library.action: Do this: rotate reviewers and vary the sample rather than reviewing the same queue indefinitely.

library.title: System Cards
library.hook: One page describing what a deployed system does and doesn't do.
library.message: Purpose, inputs, outputs, model, known limitations, oversight arrangements and owner. It's the document everyone wants and nobody writes.
library.action: Do this: write a system card for your main AI deployment. One page is enough.

library.title: Recording Intended Use
library.hook: Writing down the intended use makes misuse identifiable.
library.message: Without a stated purpose, there's no basis for saying a use is inappropriate. With one, drift becomes visible and correctable.
library.action: Do this: state the intended use and the explicitly out-of-scope uses.

library.title: Known Limitations Register
library.hook: A limitations register, kept current, shared with users.
library.message: Every deployment has known weaknesses. Documented and communicated, they're managed. Undocumented, each user discovers them individually, usually the hard way.
library.action: Do this: publish the known limitations where users will actually see them.

library.title: Version and Change History
library.hook: Record what changed, when, and who approved it.
library.message: Prompt edits, model version changes, retrieval library updates and configuration changes all alter behaviour, often with no visible deployment.
library.action: Do this: keep a change log for AI system configuration, not just code.

library.title: Data Provenance Statements
library.hook: Say where the inputs came from and under what permission.
library.message: Provenance statements matter for training data, retrieval libraries and any dataset used in evaluation. The question arrives during due diligence or an incident.
library.action: Do this: record source and permission basis for every dataset you use.

library.title: Explaining Models to Non-Experts
library.hook: Explaining models to non-experts without false simplicity.
library.message: "It's like a very fast intern" misleads in a specific direction. Better: it predicts likely text from patterns, which explains both the fluency and the fabrication.
library.action: Do this: use the prediction framing. It's accurate and it generalises.

library.title: Internal vs. External Transparency
library.hook: Decide what's published and what stays in the file.
library.message: Full detail internally, honest summaries for clients, and careful judgement publicly. Over-disclosure of system detail can enable attacks; under-disclosure erodes trust.
library.action: Do this: agree the three levels once, rather than deciding per request.

library.title: Documentation That Stays True
library.hook: Documentation decays faster than the system changes.
library.message: Written at launch and never revisited, it becomes actively misleading, which is worse than absent because people rely on it.
library.action: Do this: date every document and set a review cycle with a named owner.

library.title: Client-Facing AI Statements
library.hook: A standard description of our AI practices we can stand behind.
library.message: Clients ask, and inconsistent answers from different people look like nobody's in charge. One approved description, used by everyone.
library.action: Do this: use the standard statement rather than writing your own each time.

library.title: Responding to a Transparency Request
library.hook: Transparency requests need a route, an owner and a timescale.
library.message: They arrive from clients, regulators, journalists and individuals, and the first response sets the tone. Improvised answers create commitments.
library.action: Do this: route transparency requests through the standard process, always.

library.title: Features You Didn't Choose
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: AI arrived inside software you've used for years.
library.message: Features appear in office suites, browsers, CRMs and security tools through routine updates, without a procurement decision or a review.
library.action: Do this: check what AI features appeared in your tools this quarter.

library.title: Default-On Settings
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Check what turned itself on after the last update.
library.message: Defaults favour adoption. Summarisation, drafting, indexing and data sharing are frequently enabled by default and disclosed in release notes nobody read.
library.action: Do this: review AI settings after major updates to any business application.

library.title: Office Suite Assistants
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Office assistants read your documents, mail and calendar.
library.message: That's the point, and it means the scope of what's being processed is everything you have access to, including material you'd never deliberately upload.
library.action: Do this: understand and configure the scope before enabling it broadly.

library.title: Search and Email Summaries
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Search and email summaries quietly index everything you hold.
library.message: Convenient, and it creates a searchable derived copy of your entire mailbox in a system with its own retention and access model.
library.action: Do this: confirm the retention and access position before enabling it.

library.title: Design and Creative Tools
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Generation features inside creative tools follow the same rules.
library.message: The image generator inside your design software carries the same rights, disclosure and appropriateness questions as a standalone tool.
library.action: Do this: apply the image generation policy regardless of which tool produced it.

library.title: Analytics Platforms
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Generated insight in dashboards has no visible source.
library.message: Analytics platforms increasingly add narrative explanations of your data. They're plausible, unattributable, and quoted in meetings as findings.
library.action: Do this: treat dashboard narrative as a hypothesis, not a finding.

library.title: Security Products With AI
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Security products claim AI capability. Verify what it actually does.
library.message: Vendor descriptions range from genuine machine learning to a rules engine with a new label. It matters for what you can rely on and what you must still do.
library.action: Do this: ask specifically what the model does, on what data, with what error rate.

library.title: Consumer Devices at Work
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Assistants on phones, watches and speakers are near your conversations.
library.message: Personal devices with always-listening features in meeting rooms and offices are a disclosure risk nobody assessed, because nobody procured them.
library.action: Do this: set expectations for personal assistant devices in sensitive areas.

library.title: Reassessing an Existing Vendor
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: When a supplier adds AI features, the original review is out of date.
library.message: Your assessment covered a product that no longer exists. Data flows, sub-processors and processing locations may all have changed.
library.action: Do this: re-assess suppliers who add material AI functionality mid-contract.

library.title: Turning Things Off
library.category: Acceptable Use, Approved Tools & Shadow AI
library.hook: Sometimes policy requires turning it off, and that's harder than it sounds.
library.message: Disabling embedded AI often requires tenant-level configuration, not a user setting, and defaults reassert themselves after updates.
library.action: Do this: disable at the tenant level and verify after each major update.

library.title: Is Our Data Ready
library.hook: Before any AI project, ask honestly whether the data is ready.
library.message: Most AI failures are data failures wearing a model costume. Incomplete, inconsistent, undocumented data produces confident nonsense regardless of the model.
library.action: Do this: run the readiness assessment before committing to a build.

library.title: Completeness and Coverage
library.hook: What isn't in your data shapes every answer from it.
library.message: Missing records, unrepresented groups and periods with no coverage all produce confident answers about a world that doesn't include them.
library.action: Do this: document known gaps in coverage before anyone draws conclusions.

library.title: Duplicate and Conflicting Records
library.hook: Clean before you index, not after the complaints.
library.message: Duplicates, superseded versions and drafts all get retrieved with equal confidence. Retrieval quality is bounded by library quality, and cleaning is unglamorous.
library.action: Do this: deduplicate and remove superseded documents before indexing.

library.title: Labelling and Annotation
library.hook: Annotation consistency has to be measured, not assumed.
library.message: Different annotators apply criteria differently, and the disagreement rate determines the ceiling on model quality. Nobody checks until results are disappointing.
library.action: Do this: measure inter-annotator agreement on a shared sample before scaling.

library.title: Historical Bias in Records
library.hook: Past decisions become future recommendations.
library.message: Historical records encode who was hired, approved, promoted and served. A model trained on them reproduces those patterns with better efficiency and less visibility.
library.action: Do this: examine what your historical data encodes before training anything on it.

library.title: Data Minimisation
library.hook: Use the least data that does the job.
library.message: More data is not better if it increases exposure without improving output. Minimisation is a legal principle and a practical risk reduction.
library.action: Do this: justify each data element you include, rather than each one you exclude.

library.title: Golden Source Definition
library.hook: When two systems disagree, one of them is authoritative. Decide which.
library.message: Without a designated golden source, AI systems retrieve whichever version they find, and different users get different answers to the same question.
library.action: Do this: designate and document the authoritative source for key data.

library.title: Data Ownership
library.hook: Someone owns each dataset, and they decide what it's used for.
library.message: Without named ownership, AI projects use data because they can access it, not because they're permitted to, and nobody catches it until an audit.
library.action: Do this: get documented owner approval before using a dataset in an AI system.

library.title: Retention Before Ingestion
library.hook: Don't index what you're legally required to delete.
library.message: Retention obligations apply before ingestion. Indexing expired records creates copies you'll struggle to find when a deletion obligation is enforced.
library.action: Do this: apply retention rules to the source before building the index.

library.title: Measuring Data Quality
library.hook: Data quality metrics predict whether an AI project will work.
library.message: Completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness and accuracy, measured on the actual dataset. Poor scores predict poor outcomes reliably.
library.action: Do this: measure quality before the project starts. Share the numbers honestly.

library.title: Why We're Doing This
library.hook: An AI strategy names outcomes, not technologies.
library.message: "Adopt AI" is not a strategy. Reducing time on a specific process, improving a specific quality measure, or entering a specific market is.
library.action: Do this: state three outcomes with numbers. Everything else follows from them.

library.title: Centralised, Federated or Free
library.hook: Centralised, federated or free — pick one deliberately.
library.message: Central control is safe and slow. Federated balances both and needs real coordination. Free is fast and produces shadow systems. Each has a running cost.
library.action: Do this: name your model explicitly, so people stop guessing which one applies.

library.title: The AI Steering Group
library.hook: The steering group needs a defined remit or it becomes a status meeting.
library.message: Who decides on new use cases, exceptions, spend and risk acceptance. Without decision rights, it reviews things nobody was waiting for.
library.action: Do this: write down what the group actually decides, and what it doesn't.

library.title: Funding Model
library.hook: How AI is funded shapes what gets built.
library.message: Central funding produces showcase projects. Chargeback produces discipline and slows experimentation. Team-level spend produces sprawl. All three are defensible.
library.action: Do this: choose the model that matches your maturity, and revisit it annually.

library.title: Prioritising Use Cases
library.hook: Score use cases consistently or the loudest sponsor wins.
library.message: Value, effort, risk and readiness, applied the same way to every proposal. Without it, prioritisation reflects seniority rather than merit.
library.action: Do this: use one scoring template for every use case, without exception.

library.title: Saying No to a Use Case
library.hook: Declining a use case well matters more than declining it correctly.
library.message: An unexplained no gets escalated, worked around, or built anyway in a spreadsheet. A clear reason and an alternative usually ends the matter.
library.action: Do this: always pair a refusal with the closest permitted alternative.

library.title: Capability Building vs. Buying
library.hook: Decide which AI skills you need permanently in-house.
library.message: Evaluation, data readiness, risk assessment and vendor challenge are hard to outsource, because they require knowing your business. Implementation often isn't.
library.action: Do this: name the capabilities you'll never outsource, then hire or train for them.

library.title: Partner and Advisor Selection
library.hook: Choosing help without outsourcing your judgement.
library.message: Advisors bring speed and pattern recognition, and they bring their own preferred architecture. The decisions about risk and priority stay yours.
library.action: Do this: require any advisor to explain the option they're not recommending.

library.title: Twelve-Month Roadmap
library.hook: Sequence the roadmap so foundations come before showcases.
library.message: The register, the policy, the classification scheme and the evaluation capability are unglamorous and make everything after them possible.
library.action: Do this: put at least one foundation item in each quarter of the roadmap.

library.title: Reviewing the Strategy
library.hook: Once a year, look honestly at what didn't work.
library.message: Abandoned pilots, tools nobody uses, and projected savings that never appeared. The organisations that improve are the ones that write this down.
library.action: Do this: include a discontinued-and-why section in your annual review.

library.title: The Real Cost of Building
library.hook: Building costs more than the build.
library.message: Evaluation, monitoring, on-call, model updates, security review and the person who understands it when they leave. The development estimate is usually a third of the real cost.
library.action: Do this: cost three years of operation, not the build.

library.title: Buying a Point Solution
library.hook: A point solution delivers fast and adds integration debt.
library.message: Each specialised tool is quick to value and adds a contract, an identity, a data flow, a review cycle and another place your data lives.
library.action: Do this: count the integration and governance cost, not just the licence.

library.title: Platform vs. Best of Breed
library.hook: Platform or best of breed: price the consolidation honestly.
library.message: Platforms reduce vendor count and governance overhead, and rarely lead in any single capability. Specialists lead and multiply your surface area.
library.action: Do this: decide which capabilities genuinely need to be best in class.

library.title: Proof of Concept Discipline
library.hook: Agree what success means before the pilot starts.
library.message: Without criteria, every pilot succeeds — someone found it useful — and nothing is learned about whether to proceed.
library.action: Do this: write the success threshold and the stop condition into the pilot brief.

library.title: Avoiding Pilot Purgatory
library.hook: Promising pilots die between the trial and production.
library.message: Usually because nobody owned the transition, the security review wasn't started, or the operating cost was never established. The technology was rarely the problem.
library.action: Do this: plan the production path before the pilot begins, not after it succeeds.

library.title: Vendor Demos
library.hook: Demos run on the vendor's data for a reason.
library.message: Curated examples, tuned prompts and a happy path. Your data is messier, and that's where you learn whether the tool works.
library.action: Do this: insist on a trial with your own documents and your own edge cases.

library.title: Total Cost of Ownership
library.hook: Three-year total cost includes people, not just licences.
library.message: Administration, training, support, integration maintenance, evaluation and governance. For most AI tools, the people cost exceeds the software cost.
library.action: Do this: use the standard TCO template. Include internal time.

library.title: Exit Strategy
library.hook: Write the exit plan before you sign.
library.message: How you'd export data, in what format, what you'd lose, how long migration takes, and what it would cost. Nobody asks this at renewal because by then it's academic.
library.action: Do this: document the exit path as part of the selection decision.

library.title: Co-Development Arrangements
library.hook: Co-development raises questions the standard contract doesn't answer.
library.message: Who owns the resulting IP, who can use the training data, who's liable for the output, and what happens if either party leaves.
library.action: Do this: settle IP, data rights and liability before any joint work starts.

library.title: Reusing What We Already Have
library.hook: The capability you need may already be in a tool you own.
library.message: Organisations frequently buy an AI product that duplicates a feature already included in their existing platform, unused because nobody enabled it.
library.action: Do this: check existing licences before evaluating a new purchase.

library.title: Why People Resist
library.hook: Resistance is usually rational. Address the actual reason.
library.message: Fear about jobs, additional workload, previous broken promises about technology, and a suspicion that quality will suffer. Enthusiasm doesn't answer any of those.
library.action: Do this: ask what people are actually worried about, then respond to that.

library.title: Announcing Without Alarming
library.hook: Announce honestly, including the effect on roles.
library.message: Messaging that avoids the question produces exactly the rumour it was trying to prevent, and destroys credibility when the effect becomes visible.
library.action: Do this: say what you know and what you don't. Vagueness is read as bad news.

library.title: Voluntary Before Mandatory
library.hook: Voluntary before mandatory, wherever you can.
library.message: Imposed tools get minimal compliance. Tools people chose get advocacy. Sequencing adoption is often more important than choosing the tool.
library.action: Do this: run a genuine opt-in period before making anything required.

library.title: Manager Enablement
library.hook: Team leads answer the hard questions. Prepare them first.
library.message: Managers get asked about job security, monitoring and workload before any formal communication lands. Unprepared, they improvise, inconsistently.
library.action: Do this: brief managers a week before the announcement, with the difficult answers.

library.title: Workflow Redesign
library.hook: Adding AI to a broken process makes it faster, not better.
library.message: The bottleneck is usually a handoff, an approval or an unclear decision right. Automating the drafting step around it changes very little.
library.action: Do this: map the process first. Fix the handoff before automating the task.

library.title: Handling Job Anxiety
library.hook: Job anxiety needs honesty, not reassurance you can't back.
library.message: Promises that nothing will change are usually false and always remembered. What you can honestly say is what's decided, what isn't, and when people will know.
library.action: Do this: say what's actually decided. Don't promise outcomes you don't control.

library.title: Union and Works Council Engagement
library.hook: Consultation obligations may apply before deployment.
library.message: Where works councils or unions are involved, monitoring, performance measurement and changes to working practice frequently require consultation, not notification.
library.action: Do this: check consultation requirements before rollout, not after.

library.title: Early Wins Worth Publicising
library.hook: Choose showcases that are real and repeatable.
library.message: The impressive demo built by your most capable person, on the cleanest data, is not evidence that anyone else can do it. Showcasing it sets a false expectation.
library.action: Do this: showcase something a typical colleague achieved in typical conditions.

library.title: Sustaining Momentum
library.hook: Month six is when momentum dies.
library.message: The novelty has gone, the sponsor has moved on, and the people who adopted early have absorbed the gain. Sustaining takes deliberate effort nobody plans for.
library.action: Do this: plan the month-six activity now, while there's still enthusiasm.

library.title: Reversing a Rollout
library.hook: Sometimes you have to withdraw a tool. Do it credibly.
library.message: Explain the reason honestly — cost, risk, or it didn't work — provide the alternative, and give people time. Silent withdrawal breeds cynicism about the next rollout.
library.action: Do this: communicate the reason. "It didn't deliver" is a respectable answer.

library.title: What a Champion Does
library.hook: A champion helps colleagues and doesn't become the help desk.
library.message: The role is encouraging good practice, sharing techniques and spotting problems. It's not unpaid support, and it isn't approval authority.
library.action: Do this: write down what champions do and, importantly, what they don't.

library.title: Selecting Champions
library.hook: Pick champions for curiosity and credibility, not seniority.
library.message: The person colleagues actually ask is rarely the person on the org chart. Appointing the wrong one produces a role nobody uses.
library.action: Do this: ask teams who they already go to. Appoint that person.

library.title: Champion Onboarding
library.hook: Before someone advises a colleague, they need to know the limits.
library.message: A champion who teaches enthusiasm without the failure modes creates confident users, which is worse than uncertain ones.
library.action: Do this: require the practitioner assessment before the champion role starts.

library.title: Running an Internal Community
library.hook: Internal communities stay useful for about a month by default.
library.message: Without seeded content, a regular rhythm and someone answering questions, the channel becomes an occasional link dump nobody reads.
library.action: Do this: commit someone to running it for six months, with a weekly rhythm.

library.title: Sharing Prompts and Patterns
library.hook: Shared prompts need review before they're promoted.
library.message: A widely adopted prompt that produces subtly biased or non-compliant output scales the problem across the organisation instantly.
library.action: Do this: review contributed prompts before featuring them.

library.title: Office Hours
library.hook: A recurring slot where anyone can bring a problem works better than documentation.
library.message: Office hours surface the questions people won't put in writing and the workarounds nobody would report.
library.action: Do this: run a weekly thirty-minute open session. Keep it even when attendance dips.

library.title: Recognising Contribution
library.hook: Recognise contribution without turning it into unpaid support work.
library.message: Champions who become the unofficial help desk burn out and stop, taking their knowledge with them. Recognition needs to come with time, not just thanks.
library.action: Do this: allocate actual time for the role and account for it in workload.

library.title: Escalation From Champions
library.hook: Champions need to know when to stop advising.
library.message: Data classification questions, contract questions, incidents and anything about a person's employment. Helpfulness in these areas creates real exposure.
library.action: Do this: give champions a clear escalation list and permission to use it.

library.title: Cross-Team Show and Tell
library.hook: Show and tell should surface reusable work, not demos.
library.message: Format matters: what problem, what was tried, what didn't work, and what someone else could take. Polished demos teach nothing transferable.
library.action: Do this: require the "what didn't work" section in every presentation.

library.title: Preventing Champion Burnout
library.hook: The enthusiastic colleague who became everyone's help desk is a predictable failure.
library.message: It happens to the best champion in every organisation, usually within four months, and they rarely say anything until they stop.
library.action: Do this: check champion workload monthly. Redistribute before someone burns out.

library.title: AI as an Accessibility Tool
library.hook: For some colleagues, these tools remove a real barrier.
library.message: Drafting support, summarisation, reading assistance and structure. For people who find writing or processing dense text difficult, the benefit is substantial and personal.
library.action: Do this: make the tools available broadly. Don't gate them behind seniority.

library.title: Not Everyone Types the Same
library.hook: Prompting ability shouldn't determine who benefits.
library.message: People who write fluently get better output, which means the tool amplifies an existing advantage unless you provide templates and examples.
library.action: Do this: publish ready-made prompts for common tasks so nobody starts from blank.

library.title: Language Equity Internally
library.hook: Colleagues working in a second language gain the most and are judged the most.
library.message: AI assistance helps them produce work at the level of their thinking rather than their vocabulary, and detection tools flag their writing disproportionately.
library.action: Do this: never use AI-detection scores in any assessment of a colleague's work.

library.title: Bias Against Non-Standard English
library.hook: Output and detectors both penalise non-standard English.
library.message: Models normalise toward a particular register, and detectors flag writing that deviates from it, including that of many perfectly fluent people.
library.action: Do this: judge work on substance. Treat detector output as unreliable in principle.

library.title: Neurodiversity and Working Styles
library.hook: Support colleagues' working styles without turning it into an assumption.
library.message: AI can help with structure, focus and processing dense material. Assuming who needs that help, based on anything, is where it goes wrong.
library.action: Do this: offer the support universally. Let people choose what helps them.

library.title: Accessible Output Formats
library.hook: Generated output isn't accessible by default.
library.message: Missing structure, no alt text, colour-only distinctions and reading orders that jump. All of it passes a visual check and fails for some colleagues.
library.action: Do this: run the accessibility checker on generated documents and slides.

library.title: Digital Divide in Adoption
library.hook: Measure who's being left behind rather than guessing.
library.message: Adoption is uneven by role, location, language and confidence. The gap widens quietly and shows up later as a performance difference nobody attributes correctly.
library.action: Do this: break adoption data down by team and location. Look for the gaps.

library.title: Inclusive Examples in Training
library.hook: Training material should reflect the whole workforce.
library.message: Examples that assume a desk, a particular language, a particular seniority or a particular kind of work exclude people from the outset.
library.action: Do this: review examples for who they assume the reader is.

library.title: Assistive Technology Compatibility
library.hook: Test AI interfaces with screen readers and alternatives.
library.message: Streaming output, dynamic updates and inconsistent structure all cause problems for assistive technology, and none of it appears in a visual review.
library.action: Do this: include assistive technology testing in your release checklist.

library.title: Asking Rather Than Assuming
library.hook: Accommodation designed with people works. Designed for them, it usually doesn't.
library.message: Assumptions about what someone needs, however well-intentioned, produce support that isn't used and occasionally offends.
library.action: Do this: ask the people affected what would actually help, before building it.

library.title: Ethics Beyond Compliance
library.hook: Legal and acceptable are two different questions.
library.message: Plenty of AI applications are lawful and would embarrass us if described accurately in public. The law is the floor, not the standard.
library.action: Do this: ask both questions separately. Don't let the legal answer close the ethical one.

library.title: The Uncomfortable Test
library.hook: Would you be content for this to be described publicly, accurately?
library.message: Not the polished version — the version a journalist would write with full knowledge of what the system does and who it affects.
library.action: Do this: apply the test to your current use case. Notice any hesitation.

library.title: Who Bears the Cost
library.hook: Name who carries the risk when the system is wrong.
library.message: Often it isn't the organisation deploying it. Customers, candidates, employees and members of the public bear the cost of errors they can't see or challenge.
library.action: Do this: identify who bears the downside. Check they have a route to challenge it.

library.title: Consent and Power
library.hook: Agreement means less when refusal has consequences.
library.message: Consent from an employee, a candidate or a customer with no real alternative isn't meaningful, whatever the form says. Power asymmetry undermines the whole basis.
library.action: Do this: ask whether refusal is genuinely costless. If not, don't rely on consent.

library.title: Automating Judgement About People
library.hook: Some decisions should stay human even where automation is legal.
library.message: Judgements about a person's character, potential, honesty or suitability. Legality is not the only consideration, and these are the ones people never forget.
library.action: Do this: keep judgements about people human, and say publicly that you do.

library.title: Environmental Cost
library.hook: Heavy usage has an energy and water cost.
library.message: It's real, it's concentrated in specific locations, and it's a legitimate consideration in choosing models and designing workflows that don't run unnecessarily.
library.action: Do this: use smaller models where they're adequate. Don't run jobs you don't need.

library.title: Labour in the Supply Chain
library.hook: Someone annotated the data behind the tools we buy.
library.message: Data labelling and content moderation work is often outsourced under difficult conditions. It's a supply chain question, and it's a fair one to ask vendors.
library.action: Do this: include labour practices in vendor assessment for major AI suppliers.

library.title: Dual Use
library.hook: Capability built for defence works equally well for attack.
library.message: Detection tooling, analysis capability and automation all have obvious offensive applications. This is our sector specifically, and it deserves deliberate thought.
library.action: Do this: consider misuse potential explicitly in any security capability you build.

library.title: Raising an Ethical Concern
library.hook: Raising an ethical concern has a route, and protection.
library.message: Concerns about how a system is being used, or what it's being built for, go through a defined channel, and raising one in good faith carries no consequence.
library.action: Do this: know the route. Use it before the thing is built, not after.

library.title: Deciding Not to Build It
library.hook: Sometimes the right decision is not to build it.
library.message: Projects we stopped, and why, are worth more as teaching material than the ones that shipped. The willingness to stop is what makes the rest of this credible.
library.action: Do this: read the stopped-projects record. Notice that stopping was survivable.
